- **Spike G4 verdict: GO (2026-09-13).** The `spike-g4-determinism` workflow (run 34802164421, commit `6e7a156`) found the 10-match per-tick hash traces and both snapshot hash lists byte-identical on ubuntu, windows and macOS (ARM); with G4-b 50/50 and G4-c 20/20 already measured, the per-tick xxh3 hash is a cross-OS, cross-architecture contract and no part of the fallback is taken. The four frozen choices (hash encoding + seed, snapshot format, RNG construction, determinism rule set) go to the owner as interview items 48–51.
- **Item 48, hash encoding and seed: option 1, approved as implemented in spike G4.** Canonical little-endian byte encoding of the state tables in id order (lengths as `u32`, fixed-stride `Option` encoding, `ENCODING_VERSION = 1` first), digested by xxh3-64 under `STATE_HASH_SEED = 0x5048_4152_4D4B_4F53`. Pinned values: `digest(b"") = 0xFE1AF732B02810AD`, `digest(b"pharmakos/g4") = 0xE17026C8A5EA4D30`. Changing the seed or the version byte invalidates every golden file.
- **Item 49, snapshot format: option 1, postcard.** postcard 1.1.3 (`default-features = false`, `use-std`) with serde; every snapshot field fixed-width, `Option` as a sentinel, `SNAPSHOT_VERSION` in the bytes and checked on restore. Measured 4,563 B at tick 4800, 0.04 ms save, 0.24–0.32 ms restore, byte-identical across ubuntu/windows/macOS. Known bend of the "never serialise usize" rule: `Vec` lengths are LEB128 varints, value-identical on every target for realistic lengths; documented at the encoder. rkyv (7,160 B, heavier dependency tree) and a hand-written codec rejected.
- **Item 50, RNG construction and stream ids: option 1, approved as implemented in spike G4.** Counter-based, stateless: `draw(n) = mix64(key ^ n·GOLDEN)` with `key = mix64(k1 ^ (seat<<32) ^ sub)`, `k1 = mix64(k0 ^ tick·GOLDEN)`, `k0 = mix64(match_seed ^ stream_id·GOLDEN)`, `GOLDEN = 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15`, `mix64` = the SplitMix64 finaliser with wrapping multiplies; ranges by multiply-shift. Stream ids are explicit constants, additive only, never renumbered: Combat = 1, Spawn = 2, Map = 3. Revisit only if a future feature needs audited statistical quality (large sampled fields in the map generator).
- **Item 51, determinism rule set: option 1, approved as implemented in spike G4.** In sim crates: no `f32`/`f64`; no `as` casts (`From`/`TryFrom` with an explicit failure mode); no `HashMap`/`HashSet` (`BTreeMap`, sorted `Vec`, `imbl::OrdMap`); no wall-clock time; `overflow-checks = true` in every profile, release included, `debug-assertions = false` in release; every sort key ends in a unique id; fixed-width types only in hashed state, lengths as `u32`; no recursion. Enforced by crate-level `deny` attributes plus the workspace clippy configuration; the walled presentation module carries an explicit allow list.
- **G4 contract items 48–51 COMPLETE.** Harness part 1 may now encode them (golden determinism hashes, the lint set) as the walking skeleton's sim crate takes shape.
- **Spike G1 verdict: GO — on Windows/Vulkan/Quadro P4000 only; the Linux half of the gate (plan §3 step 8) is outstanding (2026-09-14).** Toy build in `spikes/g1-remesh` (own greedy mesher in Rust, 288 chunks of 32³, single-voxel explosions, two upload paths into Godot 4.7.2 via gdext 0.5.5), measured over 25 Godot launches and 4 headless `meshbench` passes; full numbers in `docs/spikes/G1-destruction-remesh.md` §10. Gate rows, path B, 3 × 3 600-frame repetitions: **G1-a** remesh latency p50 0 / p90 1 / p99 **1** / max 2 frames (limit p99 ≤ 3), nothing left queued; **G1-b** 20 explosions/s sustained for 3 600 frames (frame-driven, so 209–220/s wall-clock with vsync off); **G1-c** frame time p99 **5.65 ms** median of 3 (limit 16.67), max 11.0 ms, 0 of 3 600 steady-state frames over budget; ~2.6× p99 headroom, and 40 explosions/s still holds latency p99 at exactly 3. Mesher CPU ~450 µs per chunk in-engine (headless best-of-5 p99 343 µs flat / 503 µs cratered), 0.001 allocations per meshing, 16-bit indices with 10× headroom, peak heap 18.8 MiB, video memory 82.9 MiB. Path B (direct `RenderingServer` RIDs) beats path A (`ArrayMesh`) on the two clean measurements — 57 vs 84 µs per chunk upload (1.48×, non-overlapping) and 0 vs 5 798 `ArrayMesh` objects per minute — with identical geometry; frame time is a tie. Budget candidate K = 4 chunk surfaces, B = 512 KiB per frame, nearest-camera-first with an ageing term. No rung of the fallback ladder is taken. Three real bugs found and fixed, all carried into §10.12 for the skeleton: Godot 4.7's front face for triangle primitives is clockwise under `CULL_BACK` (the first vista showed the inside of the terrain) — *corrected 2026-09-14: this entry first said “counter-clockwise”, inverting the fact the plan's §10.7 records; the spike's geometry was right and only the recorded word was wrong, caught when the harness PR copied the lesson into `crates/mesher`'s crate doc*; a `Gd<Material>` dropped after `get_rid()` leaves a dangling RID that draws nothing; the in-place surface update must compare the index array, not just the counts (29 of 2 570 in-place updates in the headline run had changed indices). Also: `godot --headless` cannot take a screenshot (dummy driver), so the CI `geometry` job renders under xvfb + lavapipe and compares against a committed 1280×720 golden (0 of 921 600 pixels differ on Windows/Vulkan; lavapipe untested). Not run: Linux/Vulkan on a real GPU, D3D12 on Windows, the Defender-exclusion A/B, a vsync-on 60 Hz confirmation. Three review findings corrected the first write-up: frame times come from a raw monotonic clock, not `_process(delta)` (the physics jitter fix quantises it to 1/720 s); K = 4 has no measured frame-time justification (chosen as the smallest K meeting latency); only the mesher's p99 is a usable CI budget (the max flaps 3×). The four-part decision plan §9 asks for (upload path, budget rule, chunk size, thread + wall placement) goes to the owner as items 52–56 below.
- **Spike G1 CI green (2026-09-14, run 34823744065).** `spike-g1-remesh` passes on every job: mesher CPU budgets on ubuntu and windows, and the Linux `geometry` job under xvfb + lavapipe matches the Windows/Quadro golden (mean 0.0039/255, 1.14 % of pixels differ at all, 0.000 % by more than 32). That measures the geometry half of the cross-OS question; the Linux frame-time half is still unmeasured (no GPU runner). Four things learnt on the way, recorded in the plan's §10.12 for the skeleton's CI: a non-editor Godot loads GDExtensions only from `.godot/extension_list.cfg`, so every fresh checkout needs `godot --headless --import` first; do not hard-code the lavapipe ICD path (the loader then finds no driver and Godot silently falls back to OpenGL 3); GitHub hides job logs *and* step summaries from logged-out viewers, so CI diagnostics are published as `::notice::` annotations; and the golden was regenerated once, explained: the shot frame moved from 880 to 180, and a Quadro render and the lavapipe render both differed from the old golden by the same 4.278 % over 32.
- **Item 52, G1 cross-OS half: option 1, the single-platform frame-time GO is accepted.** Geometry is measured identical on Linux (lavapipe, run 34823744065); frame time and latency are measured on Windows/Vulkan/Quadro P4000 only, with 2.6× p99 and 3× latency headroom. The Linux frame-time half is deferred to G1's re-run against the walking skeleton under synthetic load (§2.4), where it is added if a Linux GPU machine or runner exists by then; the `frame-time` CI job stays `if: false` until a GPU runner exists. Rejected: a live-USB/dual-boot or cloud-GPU run now (half a day to a day, blocks items 53–56, a cloud card is not this card) and WSL2 (a D3D12 translation layer, so it would characterise the wrong driver).
- **Item 53, upload path: option 1, path B (direct `RenderingServer` RIDs) with path A (`ArrayMesh` + `MeshInstance3D`) kept as a build-time switch in the skeleton's bridge.** Measured: B is 1.48× cheaper per chunk upload (57 vs 84 µs), writes 77.0 vs 96.6 KB per chunk, and creates no resources against A's 5 798 `ArrayMesh` objects a minute; frame-time p99 is a tie within noise; geometry is byte-identical. The switch exists so that a retreat to A is a flag, not a rewrite, because B carries four bug classes the bridge must keep guarding against: dangling RIDs that silently draw nothing (a `Gd<Material>` dropped after `get_rid()`), the surface-format probe, the index-array equality guard before an in-place region update (counts alone are not enough: 29 of 2 570 in-place updates in the headline run had changed indices), and a colour quantisation that must match Godot byte for byte. Rejected: B only (a retreat becomes a rewrite under pressure) and A only (churn of that order is the load that shows as hitches on a larger world or a higher K, which the spike did not measure).
- **Item 54, per-frame upload budget: option 1, K = 4 chunk surfaces and B = 512 KiB per frame, and the plan's selection rule is amended to "the smallest K that meets the latency gate".** The plan's "largest K keeping frame p99 under 16.67 ms" selects unbounded, i.e. no budget; the amended rule selects K = 4 (K = 1 and 2 fail G1-a outright, K = 8 and unbounded also pass). Drain order: anything older than 2 frames first, then nearest-to-camera, ties by chunk index; a chunk re-dirtied while queued is coalesced and keeps its earliest issue frame; the first chunk of a frame always goes through even if it alone exceeds B. B = 512 KiB is one doubling above the point where B stops binding (256 KiB), a margin for a heavier future vertex format, not an optimum. Recorded honestly: no measured frame-time reason separates K = 4 from K = 8 on this machine (the maxima were noise), so the choice is structural, a bound on per-frame work; and the ageing term never fired in any run, so it ships as insurance against the drain order's starvation mode with no measurement behind it. K and B are tuning values in the rules table, stamped into the rules hash, not constants in code. Rejected: dropping the ageing term (ships a known starvation mode untested either way) and K = 8 (doubles the worst-case work the budget exists to bound while the gate is met at a third of its latency allowance).
- **Item 55, chunk size and destruction granularity: option 1, unchanged — 32³ chunks and single-voxel destruction; no rung of the G1 fallback ladder is taken.** Measured on Windows/Vulkan: dirty fan-out max 8 chunks per explosion at radius 4 (pad = light reach + 1, both derived from `LIGHT_MAX`/`LIGHT_ATTEN`), ~450 µs mesh cost per chunk, 16-bit indices with 10× headroom (6 660 vertices max against 65 536), peak heap 18.8 MiB, video memory 82.9 MiB, radius 8 at 20 explosions/s still within the gate. Caveat carried from item 52: the headroom is Windows-only; if a Linux GPU result is ever materially worse, rung 1 (2³ edit groups) is the lever, and it does not touch the sim's voxel grid. Rejected: taking rung 1 pre-emptively (gives up single-voxel destruction for a problem no measurement shows) and 16³ chunks (eight times the chunk count and draw calls, and the chunk size is a determinism-adjacent contract).
- **Item 56, mesher thread and the presentation wall: option 1, the mesher runs on the main thread, in its own walled crate `crates/mesher` (`pharmakos-mesher`).** Measured: 450 µs per chunk × K = 4 is 1.8 ms of a 16.67 ms frame against a measured frame p99 of 5.65 ms, and Godot's single-safe thread model makes path B's `RenderingServer` calls legal from `_process` with no render-thread hop; a worker pool is not needed for v1's load and would put a second thread near world state. The wall line, as G1 found it: everything up to and including the voxel edit, the dirty set and the drain order is integer; floats begin at the first vertex coordinate; nothing a float touches is read back by the sim. The mechanism: `crates/mesher` takes integer chunk data in and produces vertex buffers out, is listed in `WALLED_PACKAGES` (and the `clippy.toml` header), is depended on by `client-gdext` and never by `sim`, `plan-core`, `verifier`, `operator` or `gateway` (`wall-guard` enforces it), and links without gdext so the headless CPU proxy and the CI geometry check can reuse it. The spike's per-file `#![deny(clippy::float_arithmetic)]` shape does not transfer. This resolves the AGENTS.md §3 placeholder for the mesher; the `math` crate question stays open for the skeleton. Adding the crate is a §5 contract change, approved here; it lands as a small harness PR at the walking skeleton together with the AGENTS.md crate-map edit. Rejected: the mesher inside `client-gdext` (breaks the thin-client rule and nothing headless can reuse it without linking gdext) and a worker pool from the start (no measurement asks for it, and path B's uploads stay on the main thread regardless).
- **G1 decision items 52–56 COMPLETE (2026-09-14).** Spike G1 is closed: GO, path B with an A switch, K = 4 / B = 512 KiB under the amended rule, 32³ chunks and single-voxel destruction unchanged, main-thread mesher in a walled `mesher` crate. Next: spikes G2 + P3 (pathing and travel estimates) and G3′ (segment budget), then the walking skeleton.
- **Spike G2+P3 verdict: GO at cluster 32 — the editor may promise a travel time, not a range; the cross-OS half of step 9 (path identity on Linux) is pending the first CI run (2026-09-14).** Toy build in `spikes/g2-pathing` (own HPA* over a 2.5D surface graph of 384×384×64 — 147 456 columns, one node per column; integer octile costs 10/14 plus a climb surcharge of 4; a hand-written binary heap ordered by the total order (f, h, node_id); dense generation-stamped scratch, no `HashMap`, no floats, no `as`, no recursion, `u32` ids, `i32` costs with the map's maximum asserted at start-up; cluster = chunk footprint, entrances rescanned and intra-cluster edges rebuilt eagerly per dirtied cluster plus one CSR rebuild per tick; a union-find connectivity oracle answers “no path” before any search; the estimator is the abstract search alone with ticks = ceil(cost / 3)); no dependencies at all; 42 tests, including A* against exhaustive Dijkstra on 1 000 pairs with 0 mismatches and a test that the library reads no clock. Full numbers in `docs/spikes/G2-P3-pathing.md` §9. Gate rows at cluster 32 (three runs of 20 000 repaths under 20 craters/s, 10 000 estimates, 2 000 accuracy pairs): **G2-a** repath p99 cold 1.80 / 1.84 / 1.84 ms (limit 5), max 2.2–4.1 ms; **P3-a** estimate p99 0.82 ms (limit 1), 0.887 ms within the worst band (>256 cells); **P3-b** estimate vs walked |error| p90 **2.6 %** (limit 15), 1.3 % on routes over 256 cells, and never optimistic — the signed error equals the absolute error at every percentile, because the estimate prices the unsmoothed refinement and the smoother only removes cost. Cluster sweep: 16 passes G2-a (1.08 ms) and P3-b (3.8 %) but its estimate p99 inside the >256-cell band is 1.076 ms against an aggregate of 0.972, so it fails P3-a on exactly the routes an ETA is read for, and its cluster is no longer a chunk; 64 fails P3-a outright (1.43 ms, every band) and pays 18.5 ms p99 to repair one dirtied cluster. Accuracy improves as clusters coarsen (3.8 → 2.6 → 1.6 %), so latency, not accuracy, is what fixes the size. One abstract level: endpoint insertion is 91 % of a median query's expansions (1 774 of 1 943), so a second level could save at most 9 %. Repair, not search, is what a walker actually waits for: cold + the tick's repair share p99 2.95 ms, max 8.9 ms; 1.48 ms p50 per dirtied cluster, 1.35 clusters per crater, 0.50 ms per CSR rebuild — about 2.5 ms per crater. Peak demand 1 474 repaths per game-second against 1 235/s of single-thread throughput, which is plan §6's case for a deterministic per-tick repath cap. “No path” fires on 4.5 % of repaths and costs 0.0001 ms; one walker was sealed in by its own destruction, which the sim needs as a designed state. Recorded separately and not part of the gate: fog (×1.5 per abstract edge when either endpoint is unknown) |error| p90 48.6 %, capped at +50 % over the clear estimate; dynamic terrain (the estimate at issue against the tick of actual arrival while craters fall) |error| p90 12.5 %, p99 62.5 %, so the gate's “on static terrain” is load-bearing. Memory: 4.1 MiB of structures, 11.2 MiB peak live heap, 14.5 MiB peak working set read from outside the process. Same-machine path identity: four bench runs walked byte-identical routes and two `--hash-paths` files (3 200 hashes covering the pristine map and 300 crater repairs) are identical under `cmp`, digest `ef29afabb1d26148` at cluster 32. Measured differently from the plan, stated in §9.9: fog is priced per abstract edge, not per cell (the per-cell count is the refinement the estimator may not do); “cold” means the first repath against a CSR rebuilt this tick, because the design holds no per-query cache to be cold; the second level was bounded from the expansion split rather than built; the generator's columns are 100 % walkable, so the graph's structure lives in the 1-voxel step rule (20 craters/s removed 131 356 directed steps and shattered the largest component from 130 937 to 35 461 cells); peak RSS was sampled from outside because the spike may take no dependency. One structural fix identified and deliberately not built: a corner entrance, which would remove most of the ≤32-cell band's error (p90 9.2 %, max 66.6 %). 28 review findings over three lenses, all applied: four blockers (the generation counter was reset without re-zeroing the stamps, so a query after a resize could read stale state; cold/warm was a label rather than a measurement; `--hash-paths` covered only static queries, not the repair path; the CI `path-identity` job inherited a working directory that does not exist on its runner), the rest majors and minors including the CI thresholds, which now assert the G2-a gate itself (5 ms) and 2.5 ms for the estimate as regression alarms. Tuning values the numbers depend on, all to become rules-table data at S3: 10 / 14 / 4, speed 3 cost units per tick with ceil, headroom 2, long-run 6, lookahead 16, cluster 32, crater radius 3. The decision plan §8 asks for — the headline and its five parts — goes to the owner as items 57–62 below.
- **Spike G2+P3 CI green (2026-09-14, run 34861229486).** `spike-g2-pathing` passes on every job on the first run: fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, 42 tests, the bench and accuracy gates on ubuntu and windows, and the `path-identity` job — Linux and Windows agree on all 3 203 lines of the path-hash file at every cluster size (digests `d98ba7776dc48e9c` / `ef29afabb1d26148` / `8daf1375f13e8619` for 16 / 32 / 64), which is the cross-OS half of plan §3 step 9 and closes the last open measurement: the (f, h, node_id) total order holds across operating systems. The hosted runners also reproduced the gate: ubuntu cold repath p99 1.37 ms and estimate p99 0.67 ms, windows 2.21 ms and 0.98 ms, all at the same routes digest `360bb858b87df6e9` across the three repeats on each OS; the Windows runner is the slower of the two and comes within 2 % of the 1 ms estimate budget, which is why the CI estimate alarm sits at 2.5 ms. The G1 lessons carried over cleanly: concurrency + timeouts, assertions inside the binaries, diagnostics as `::notice::` annotations read through the check-runs API, `python` via setup-python on both runners.
- **Item 57, the G2+P3 headline: option 1, the editor promises a travel time, rendered as a number.** Measured on static terrain at cluster 32: estimate vs walked |error| p90 2.6 % against the 15 % budget, 1.3 % on routes over 256 cells, and never optimistic (the estimate prices the unsmoothed refinement and the smoother only removes cost), so a unit is never later than promised on the terrain the playbook was sealed against. Two rules the editor must honour, carried into item 61's contract: a short route's ETA is rounded generously or shown in whole seconds (the ≤32-cell band has p90 9.2 % and max 66.6 %, i.e. one second on a two-second route), and a fogged leg is drawn as the upper bound it is, not as an ETA (48.6 % p90 under the ×1.5 rule). Recorded honestly: the promise is made on static terrain and the Push is not static — under 20 craters/s the same estimate is 12.5 % p90 and 62.5 % p99 against actual arrival, and the player sees the discrepancy at arrival, not the caveat. Plan §6's fallback (“show ranges; favour arrival triggers”) is not taken in any part; the playbook vocabulary keeps its clock-phrased conditions alongside the arrival-phrased ones. Rejected: a range anyway (discards a measurement 5.8× under budget and drifts the vocabulary towards arrival triggers for no measured reason) and a number on clear routes with a band on contested ones (two renderings to teach, and “contested” is not decidable by the estimator without the simulation work §3 forbids; the decidable part, fog, is settled in item 61).
- **Item 58, cluster size and abstract levels: option 1, clusters of 32×32 cells (one chunk footprint) and a single abstract level.** Measured at 32: repath p99 1.84 ms, estimate p99 0.82 ms (0.887 ms inside the >256-cell band), error p90 2.6 % — the only size that passes all three assertions including on long routes. A cluster equals a chunk, so a crater's dirty chunk list is its dirty cluster list with no translation; repairing one dirtied cluster costs 1.48 ms p50 / 3.30 ms p99, 1.35 clusters per crater, plus 0.50 ms per tick for the CSR rebuild. One level, on evidence rather than intuition: endpoint insertion is 91 % of a median query's expansions (1 774 of 1 943) and is cluster-local by construction, so a second abstract level could save at most 9 %; coarsening to 64 is the same trade and it breaks the 1 ms budget. Recorded honestly: 32 leaves 18 % of the estimate budget and the band max already touches 1.03 ms; the hosted Windows runner came within 2 % of the budget, so a slower target machine or a busier map is the risk, and the lever if it bites is the endpoint sweep (cache the commander's start transitions while it stands still; goals are usually static beacons), not the abstract graph. If a later map is much larger than 384², re-check the ratio of abstract expansions to endpoint-sweep expansions before revisiting a second level. Rejected: 16 (estimate p99 1.076 ms inside the >256-cell band — fails P3-a on exactly the routes an ETA is read for — twice the graph to repair, the worst dynamic error at 16.3 % p90, and a cluster that is no longer a chunk), 64 (fails P3-a by 43 % in every band and pays 18.5 ms p99 per cluster repair), and 32 with a second level built as insurance (a second deterministic graph to repair per crater for a measured ceiling of 9 %).
- **Item 59, the integer cost model: option 1, `STEP_CARDINAL = 10`, `STEP_DIAGONAL = 14`, `CLIMB_SURCHARGE = 4` per one-voxel step up or down, `MOVE_COST_PER_TICK = 3`, and cost → ticks by ceiling (`ticks = (cost + 2) / 3`), all four as rules-table data stamped into the rules hash.** 10/14 is the octile approximation, so no square root and no float anywhere and the heuristic stays admissible and consistent; ceiling is the rounding that keeps the estimate one-sided (never optimistic, the property item 57 rests on) and is what the walk integrator is tested against; the map's maximum path cost is 2 654 208 against `i32::MAX`, 810× headroom, asserted at start-up. Recorded honestly: ceiling adds up to one tick (50 ms) of pessimism per query, a systematic floor under the measured 0.7 % median bias; the surcharge has no gameplay evidence behind it and is a tuning question for S3. Rejected: a finer 100/141 scale (ten times the accumulated magnitude for no measured gain — the octile error is not what limits accuracy, the missing corner entrance is), an asymmetric up/down surcharge (makes the graph directed, which the CSR and the connectivity oracle would both have to learn; raise as tuning if climbing should feel expensive), and round-to-nearest (can round a walk down by up to half a tick, breaking never-late).
- **Item 60, incremental repair: option 1, cluster = chunk footprint, repaired eagerly at edit time — rescan the dirtied clusters' entrances plus the neighbours whose border transition set actually changed, rebuild their intra-cluster edges, then one CSR + connectivity rebuild per tick.** “Affected neighbour” is computed, not assumed; three tests pin it (repair equals a from-scratch build, equals the conservative all-neighbours set, and holds at every cluster size). Measured at 32: 1.48 ms p50 / 3.30 ms p99 per dirtied cluster, 1.35 clusters per crater, 0.50 ms per tick for the rebuild — about 2.5 ms per crater, 5 % of one core at 20 craters/s. Two riders taken with it, both deterministic: (a) a per-tick repath cap served by a round-robin queue ordered (seat, beacon, unit), because peak demand was 1 474 repaths per game-second against 1 235/s of single-thread throughput (plan §6's named G2-a lever, taken pre-emptively as a bound on per-tick work, cap value a tuning number for S3); (b) “sealed in” is a designed unit state — park, report to the seat — not a repath loop, because one walker at cluster 32 and seven at 16 were buried by their own destruction and “no path” fires on 4.5 % of repaths (answered by the union-find oracle in 0.0001 ms). Recorded honestly: repair, not search, is what a walker waits for — cold repath plus the tick's repair share is 2.95 ms p99 and 8.9 ms max — and at 20 craters/s this competes with the mesher and the rest of the tick, whose budget G3′ has not yet fixed. Rejected: lazy repair on first query (turns an amortised cost into a spike when many units repath at once, and makes graph contents depend on query order — a determinism hazard for hashed state), finer-than-cluster granularity (the intra rebuild is the expensive half and needs a dependency structure that does not exist; 1.48 ms does not justify it), and running on a stale path for bounded ticks (G2-a passed 2.7×; buys nothing and shows as walking into craters). Decided under the owner's standing instruction of 2026-09-14 to take the recommended option until told otherwise.
- **Item 61, the estimator's API and error contract: option 1, a tick count, not a range.** `estimate(world, clusters, scratch, start, goal, fog) -> Option<Estimate { cost, ticks, legs }>`; `None` means no route and is answered by the connectivity oracle before any search (a normal, cheap result — a moat seals you in as well); `legs` is the number of abstract edges crossed, which is what the editor uses to draw the polyline. The estimator is the abstract search alone: it never refines, never steps, never forks (AGENTS.md §3 rule 2). Error contract, written into the gateway's `docs` output: within ±15 % at p90 of walked time on static terrain (measured 2.6 %; the margin is S3's to spend on the difference between the toy and the real sim, not accuracy to bank), and **never optimistic** — the editor's rounding depends on that property, so it is part of the contract, not an implementation detail. Fog: priced ×1.5 per abstract edge when either endpoint cell is unknown (integer `cost * 3 / 2`), an approximation of §11's per-cell rule chosen because counting unknown cells is the refinement the estimator may not do; measured |error| p90 48.6 %, capped at +50 % over the clear estimate. What the editor may render from a fogged leg: a dashed leg (spec section 13) labelled as an upper bound, never as an ETA — the route's total shows the clear legs' time plus the fogged bound, marked as a bound. Short routes: rounded generously or shown in whole seconds (item 57). No estimate cache: P3-a passes with 18 % headroom and a cache is hashed state that has to be invalidated identically on every platform; a per-(start cluster, goal cluster) cache invalidated on repair stays plan §6's named P3-a fallback. Rejected: always returning a (low, high) pair (discards the measurement, and the “high” would be the arbitrary ×1.5 bound) and a cache now. Decided under the owner's standing instruction of 2026-09-14.
- **Item 62, the total-order tiebreak — part of the determinism contract alongside items 48–51: option 1, search nodes are ordered by `(f, h, node_id)`, ascending in all three, in a hand-written binary min-heap.** `f = g + h`; ascending `h` among equal `f` prefers the node further along; `node_id` last makes the order total, so no two distinct nodes ever compare equal and the pop sequence is a function of the graph and nothing else. Every other sort key in pathing — entrances, neighbours, dirty sets, the repath queue — ends in a unique id; open set is the heap, closed set and g-scores are dense arrays indexed by `u32` node id with generation stamps (no `HashMap`, no `usize` in anything hashed), costs are `i32`, no recursion. Measured: `the_tiebreak_is_total_under_neighbour_permutation` passes; four bench runs at cluster 32 walked byte-identical routes; and CI run 34861229486's `path-identity` job found Linux and Windows identical on all 3 203 lines at every cluster size (digests `d98ba7776dc48e9c` / `ef29afabb1d26148` / `8daf1375f13e8619`). Open: macOS is not in this spike's matrix; G4's matrix covers it and S3's certification on real code inherits that. Rejected: `(f, node_id)` only (still total but discards the goal-ward preference and expands more nodes for the same answer) and `std::collections::BinaryHeap` (no order among equal keys, and the order it does produce depends on insertion history and the std implementation — the trap plan §5 names; the total-order key makes the container irrelevant, which is the point). Decided under the owner's standing instruction of 2026-09-14.
- **G2+P3 decision items 57–62 COMPLETE (2026-09-14).** Spike G2+P3 is closed: GO at cluster 32; the editor promises a travel time; 10 / 14 / 4 / 3-per-tick with ceiling as rules-table data; eager chunk-footprint repair with a deterministic per-tick repath cap and a designed sealed-in state; the estimator returns ticks under a never-optimistic ±15 % contract with fog as a labelled upper bound; the `(f, h, node_id)` total order joins the determinism contract. Structural fix carried to S3, not built: a corner entrance per cluster. Next: spike G3′ (segment budget), then the walking skeleton.
- **Spike G3′ verdict: GO on G3′-b, the binding constraint; G3′-a conditional on the per-tick repath cap; the 3/5/8 ladder affordable as written; Linux/macOS and the three-OS hash-stream comparison pending the first CI run (2026-09-14).** Toy build in `spikes/g3-tick-budget`, started from a copy of G4's toy sim (same fixed-point types, canonical encoding + xxh3 under the item-48 seed, counter-based RNG streams, kill-credit rule) and extended to run-time counts: eleven named phases — broadphase (CSR uniform grid rebuilt by counting sort, r² queries in Q32.32), programs, movement, combat, kill_credit, power, quartermaster, decision (every 5th tick, all seats), voxels (32³ copy-on-write chunk store, 20 craters/s), hash (full and incremental), and a `pathing` phase that stands in for G2: a real integer path-follow over the unit table plus G2's measured repath (0.77 ms, 1.84 ms once in a hundred), cluster repair (2.5 ms per crater) and CSR rebuild (0.5 ms per tick) charged as a calibrated, state-free busy loop; G4's pinned dependencies only; 25 tests including the incremental hash equal to the from-scratch fold and sensitive to every field, the tick reading no clock, broadphase equal to brute force, and the hash stream identical across runs. Full numbers in `docs/spikes/G3prime-segment-budget.md` §9. Measured with overflow checks on, pinned to one core from outside, clocks recorded (the pinned core held 108–112 % of nominal, no thermal trend), Defender not excluded, 2 000 warm-up + 9 600 measured ticks, median of three: **G3′-b** mean tick 10.620 ms, 4.708× real time (limit 12.5 ms / 4×), 15 % of headroom; **G3′-a** tick p99 **56.2 ms** with the per-tick repath cap unbounded (limit 25 — FAIL), **16.5 ms** at a cap of 16 (PASS), 28.1 ms at 32 (FAIL); **G3′-c** met at world totals (4 seats, 300 units, 40 beacons); at per-seat counts (1 200 units / 160 beacons) the tick is 33.6 ms mean and 215.9 ms p99 and no tuning value recovers it. Two health warnings that govern how every number is read: (1) **96.5 % of the gate tick is charged, not measured** — the tick minus the pathing substitute is 0.27 ms, so the spike answers “does G2's pathing load plus a sim fit in a tick”, not “is the sim fast”; (2) **the G3′-a verdict is a readout of one unmeasured constant**, the repath burst frequency — G2 reported the burst's size (74 repaths in one tick) but not its rate; at a modelled 1-in-64 the p99 is a burst tick (56 ms), at 1-in-128 it is not (12.1 ms), and the mean moves 2.3 % across the whole range. That constant is a PLACEHOLDER for the owner with G2 at S2's exit; until then G3′-a is quoted as conditional, and the lever that settles it is the per-tick repath cap item 60 already defines (sweep: 8 is unsustainable — the queue never drains and 14 % of the work is dropped; 16 sustainable and passing; 32 and unbounded failing; stability floor 9.45, p99 ceiling 15.4 after the reserve). Per-phase, gate configuration: pathing 10.35 ms (96.5 %, of which the real path-follow is under 0.2 ms), broadphase 0.20 ms, hash 0.018 ms, everything else under 0.01 ms each. Full vs incremental hash: identical digest `44217aea12b1af6a` over 9 600 ticks; incremental re-encodes 7.641 of 8 tables (every live table is dirty on essentially every tick) and saves 0.001–0.0025 ms, inside the hash phase's own run-to-run spread; hashing the chunk store's 9.4 MB of bytes instead of its 288 per-chunk digests would cost 0.834 ms, 43× the whole eight-table hash. Cost model (destruction-off sweep for the sim's own terms): 1 022 ns per unit per tick, 1 234 ns per unit per crater-per-second for G2's repath load, 6 960 ns per voxel edit for the chunk store, 1 041 ns per decision tick per seat, fixed term 0.47 ms that is entirely G2's CSR rebuild; the beacon term did not resolve and is published as a bracket [231, 3 159] ns; the unit cost is measurably super-linear (+34 % quadratic share at 600 units) and the broadphase is the phase to watch. Provisional per-map power budget: **190 kW** = 190 affordable units world-wide at a PLACEHOLDER 1 kW per unit and a PLACEHOLDER 40 % reserve at 20 craters/s (446 at 10/s, 55 at 40/s — the destruction rate and the budget must be set together at S2's exit). Drift over the full 8-minute segment: none (p50 0 ‰, mean −7 ‰ minute 1 to minute 8); 0.003 allocations per tick; peak working set 15.5 MiB, read from inside via a hand-declared `K32GetProcessMemoryInfo` and from outside via PowerShell, agreeing to 8 KiB; overflow checks cost 2.1 % on the mean and 2.2 % on the p99 with a byte-identical hash stream. Four hash streams (full, incremental, cap 16, checks off) byte-identical over 9 600 ticks; the cross-OS comparison is the CI `hash-identity` job. Measured differently from the plan, stated in §9.15: Linux and macOS not run locally (the workflow was not installed at measurement time; the cross-platform figure with signal is `tick_minus_pathing_mean_ms`, because the charged phase reproduces G2's milliseconds on every machine by construction); the repath cap measured for what it costs, not what it picks (item 60's round robin has no subject in a substitute); the fixed overhead the fit returns is G2's CSR rebuild, so S2 must not charge it twice; kill_credit settled only 37 deaths; one map, one seed. One harness defect found and fixed from outside the binary: the pathing calibration in the first 120 ms of the process read a ramping clock, so the driver now pre-warms the pinned core for 6 s; the ±3 % residual is reported, not smoothed. 40 review findings over three lenses, all applied (blockers: the burst frequency deciding the verdict was an unsourced constant, now a named PLACEHOLDER with a sensitivity table; the incremental hash never skipped a table at the gate, now measured with the table counts published; the linearity test ran on the one sweep where linearity was guaranteed by construction, now taken from the destruction-off sweep). The decision plan §8 asks for — its five parts, plus §1's open question and the repath cap — goes to the owner as items 63–69 below.
- **Spike G3′ CI green (2026-09-14, run 34908269505).** `spike-g3-tick-budget` passes on every job: fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, 25 tests, tickbench at the gate configuration and the cost-model sweep on ubuntu, windows and macos (aarch64), and the `hash-identity` job — **all three operating systems agree on all 9 600 per-tick hashes**, digest `44217aea12b1af6a`, with the full and incremental modes identical on each; that is a second, independent three-OS determinism trace on top of G4's, and it covers a 384×384×64 copy-on-write chunk store under 9 600 craters, a CSR broadphase, per-seat power and treasury passes and the kill-credit apportionment. The hosted runners reproduced the shape of the local result — mean tick 10.50 ms ubuntu / 10.59 windows / 11.56 macos (all ≥ 4× real time), p99 55.6–56.4 ms at an unbounded repath cap and 15.2–16.9 ms at a cap of 16, provisional budget 169–179 kW — but the totals agree across platforms by construction, because the charged pathing phase reproduces G2's milliseconds on every machine; the figure with signal is the tick minus that phase: **0.231 ms ubuntu, 0.252 ms windows, 0.229 ms macos**, so plan §3 step 7's “budget set by the slower first-class OS” reads Windows, by 9 % on 2 % of the tick. The first run for the spike commit (34908177661) was cancelled by the concurrency group when the verdict entry was pushed a minute later — every push to `main` had been re-running every spike workflow — so the four spike workflows now carry a `paths` filter and only run when their own spike directory or workflow file changes.
- **Item 63, what the G3′ gate row counts: option 1, world totals — “4 seats, 300 units, 40 beacons” means 300 units and 40 beacons across the whole match (75 and 10 a seat at four seats; about 100 units a seat in a three-seat v1 match).** It is the reading the spike measured as primary, it passes G3′-b with 15 % of headroom, and it is the only reading under which a usable power budget exists: at per-seat counts (1 200 units / 160 beacons) the tick is 33.6 ms mean and 215.9 ms p99, 2.7× over G3′-b and 8.6× over G3′-a, and no tuning value recovers that. Recorded honestly: this is the reading generous to the engine; a later design that wants a seat to field 300 units re-derives the budget rather than scaling it, because the broadphase grew 7.2× for a 4× unit count. Rejected: per-seat counts (a different engine, and the gate would be failed rather than conditional) and leaving it open until S2 (the per-map power budget is the map generator's input and the generator is built at the walking skeleton, so “open” means a number that may move by 4× under a generator already written). Owner's explicit answer, 2026-09-14.
- **Item 64, the tick's cost model: option 1, adopt the five numbers as the skeleton's provisional model, in the shape §9.6 of the plan publishes them.** `a0` = 1 022 ns per unit per tick for the sim's own work (destruction off), `d` = 1 234 ns per unit per crater-per-second for G2's repath load, 6 960 ns per voxel edit for the chunk store, 1 041 ns per decision tick per seat, and a fixed term of 0.47 ms that is entirely G2's CSR rebuild (0.50 ms) with the sim's own overhead lost in the noise beneath it — so S2 must not charge the CSR rebuild twice. The beacon term did not resolve and is carried as a bracket, [231, 3 159] ns per beacon per tick; it cancels out of the budget arithmetic. The chunk-store cost of a crater and its pathing consequence keep different names. The hosted runners corroborate the shape (ubuntu `a0` 885, `d` 1 272; windows 952, 1 276). Recorded honestly: `a0` is a linear fit over a series that is measurably super-linear (+34 % quadratic share at 600 units), so it under-states the marginal unit above 300 and over-states it below — a budget input, not a law. Rejected: publishing only the phase means with no fitted model (step 5 then has no arithmetic and the power budget becomes a guess) and carrying a fitted quadratic term (over-fitting a six-point sweep of a synthetic broadphase whose cell size the real one need not share; the shape is the finding, the coefficient is not). Decided under the owner's standing instruction of 2026-09-14.
- **Item 65, the provisional per-map power budget: option 1, 190 kW — 190 affordable units world-wide at a PLACEHOLDER 1 kW per unit and a PLACEHOLDER 40 % reserve, at 20 craters per second — and the destruction rate is recorded in the same decision, because it moves the answer from 6 873 units at zero to 446 at 10/s, 190 at 20/s and 55 at 40/s.** Arithmetic, every input named (plan §9.7): 12.5 ms mean budget less the 40 % reserve = 7.5 ms; minus the fixed 0.47 ms and the unit-free crater cost at 20/s (2.4 ms) = 4.6 ms; divided by the cost of one unit at 20/s (`a0` + 20·`d` ≈ 25.7 µs) = 190 units; times 1 kW per unit = 190 kW. The p99 constraint does not reduce to a unit count — its tail is a repath burst on a single tick — and solves instead for the per-tick repath cap (item 69). Provisional in a strong sense: two PLACEHOLDERs sit inside the number (the reserve, owner at S2's exit; kW per unit, a section 19 Tuning value at S1/S2) and the third input, G2's repath load, is charged rather than measured; superseded by S2's exit measurement, which sets the map generator's real ceiling. Cross-referenced from spec section 19's Tuning row for kW. Rejected: the quiet-map figure (a map supplying power for a unit count the tick cannot carry the moment destruction starts, which is the configuration the game is always in), deferring the number entirely to S2 (the generator built at the skeleton needs a ceiling, and “no number” is an implicit one nobody wrote down), and a thinner reserve (a tick that is 96 % substituted flatters the real one; if anything 40 % is thin). Decided under the owner's standing instruction of 2026-09-14.
- **Item 66, full or incremental per-tick state hash — part of the determinism contract alongside items 48–51: option 1, full.** Re-hash every table every tick, in declared order, into a reused buffer; the chunk store enters the hash as its 288 per-chunk digests, refreshed only for chunks an edit touched, never as its bytes. Measured: full and incremental produce the identical digest `44217aea12b1af6a` over 9 600 ticks on all three OSes; incremental re-encodes 7.641 of 8 tables at the gate configuration because every live table is dirty on essentially every tick, and saves 0.001–0.0025 ms — 0.02 % of the gate tick and inside the hash phase's own run-to-run spread; hashing the chunk store's 9.4 MB of bytes instead of its digests would cost 0.83 ms, 43× the whole eight-table hash and three times the entire non-pathing tick. The reason is structural, not the saving: an incremental scheme buys its saving with a dirty flag on every write site in the sim, forever, on the determinism artefact itself, and a missed flag produces a wrong hash rather than a slow one — a desync found days later on another operating system. Rejected: incremental at whole-table granularity (what the spike built; nothing to skip in a live tick) and at finer granularity (strictly more flags to miss for a saving there is no evidence of; the one fine-grained scheme that stays, per-chunk voxel digests, is not a dirty-flag scheme but the encoding itself). Decided under the owner's standing instruction of 2026-09-14.
- **Item 67, the table layout and broadphase the skeleton starts from: option 1, keep both, with the caveat written down.** Vec-backed structure-of-arrays tables with the counts fixed at construction (the spike ran 300 and 1 200 units from the same code with zero allocations per tick), and a CSR uniform grid over the map footprint rebuilt every tick by counting sort — cell edge equal to the largest query radius so a radius query touches at most 3 × 3 cells, rebuild O(items + cells), allocation-free after construction. The caveat: the cell size is a tuning value tied to unit density, and the query is super-linear in unit count (+34 % quadratic share at 600 units, marginal cost per unit up 72 % across the sweep), so the structure that is 28 % of the quiet tick today is 47 % at twice the load — the phase to watch before the unit ceiling doubles. Rejected: a two-level or hierarchical grid now (a solution to a problem the gate load does not have at 0.22 ms, and a second structure to keep deterministic and hashed), a BVH or a sorted-by-cell array (the BVH's rebuild is not O(items + cells) and is hard to make allocation-free; the sorted array is what the CSR already is; neither addresses the mechanism, which is more candidates per 3 × 3 neighbourhood as density rises), and `imbl` persistent maps for hot tables as G4's toy used for kill credit (small-allocation traffic back in the hot loop, which is exactly what plan §5's allocator row says makes the budget platform-dependent). Decided under the owner's standing instruction of 2026-09-14.
- **Item 68, the 3 / 5 / 8-minute segment ladder: option 1, affordable as written; keep it.** A full 8-minute segment at the gate configuration shows no drift: p50 0 ‰ and mean −7 ‰ from minute 1 to minute 8, and +16 ‰ / +11 ‰ with destruction off, which is scheduling noise on a machine with turbo enabled; the copy-on-write chunk store (9 600 craters, 467 000 voxels removed) and the accumulating wrecks cost nothing measurable, and the three hosted OSes agree (ubuntu −5 ‰, windows 0 ‰; macos noisier but flat on the p50). Recorded honestly: the check covers this tick — the chunk store's `Arc` sharing and the wreck population are in it — but not process-wide memory growth from a mesher, a renderer, a gateway or a verifier, which S2 re-measures. Rejected: shortening the ladder (the spec's §6 fallback; it discards a measurement that came back clean, and it interacts with the fun gate, whose own fallback ladder starts with a shorter Push ladder — if both gates ever point that way the change is made once, deliberately, not pre-emptively here). Decided under the owner's standing instruction of 2026-09-14.
- **Item 69, the per-tick repath cap's value — the tuning number item 60 left open: option 1, 16 repaths per tick (window 15–16), re-derived at S2's exit once the burst frequency is a measurement.** The lever the G3′ measurement actually needs, and neither of the spec's two fallback levers: 16 is sustainable (mean backlog 2.85 over a full segment, no growth, 100 % served) and turns G3′-a from FAIL (56.2 ms p99 unbounded) to PASS (16.5 ms) at no measurable cost on the mean; 15.4 is the ceiling the p99 arithmetic gives after the 40 % reserve; 9.45 — G2's mean demand per crater at one crater a tick — is the stability floor below which the queue never drains. Served in the round-robin order item 60 fixed, (seat, beacon, unit), so which repaths a busy tick defers is a function of the state and nothing else. Recorded honestly: the window is narrow and both ends move with constants this spike did not measure (the burst frequency, G2's per-repath cost on real code), and the cap was measured for what it costs, not for what it picks. Rejected: 32 (fails G3′-a at 28.1 ms p99), 8 or anything below about 9.5 (the cheapest row in the sweep and not a configuration — the backlog grew by 3 092 over the segment and 14 % of the work was dropped for ever; a cap below mean demand buys a cheap tick by not doing the work), and no cap (a tick that misses its deadline outright whenever a burst lands). Decided under the owner's standing instruction of 2026-09-14.

All four stack spikes (G4, G1, G2+P3, G3′) are closed. - **Item 70, the `math` crate question (AGENTS.md §3 placeholder, walking-skeleton opening): option 1, no separate `math` crate — the integer newtypes (`Fx`, `Sq`, `Angle` + LUT, HP, `$`, `kW`, `Tick`, `Ms`), the RNG streams, the canonical encoding and the state hash stay as modules inside `pharmakos-sim`, and HPA* and the map generator stay there too.** Reasons: the only crates that need those types besides the sim are `plan-core`, `verifier` and `gateway`, and each already depends on `pharmakos-sim` with `default-features = false` for exactly the snapshot and knowledge types this would split out, so a `math` crate would add a crate without removing a dependency edge; the determinism contract (items 48–51, 62, 66) then stays in one crate, which is what makes “the determinism code” a nameable contract path for AGENTS.md §5 and `cargo xtask ci`; and the one consumer that must not reach the sim — the walled mesher — needs none of them (its input is integer chunk data and its output is float vertex buffers, and `client-gdext` talks to the sim only through the gateway). Recorded honestly: the verifier and plan-core compile the whole sim crate to get a handful of types, which costs build time and keeps the sim's stepping API within reach — the research-guard and the “no dry runs” review rule (§3 rule 2) are the mitigation, not the type system. Revisit if the skeleton finds the verifier's build time or its temptation to step the sim to be a real problem; the split is additive then (a `math` crate the sim re-exports) and costs nothing now. The AGENTS.md §3 placeholder is resolved by this item and item 56 together and is removed in the item-56 harness PR. Rejected: a `math` crate now (a second home for contract code, two crates for every contract rule to name, and no dependency edge it actually removes). Decided under the owner's standing instruction of 2026-09-14.

The tag keeps every spike readable and checkable (`git worktree add ../pharmakos-spikes spike-end`), and an agent re-writing the mesher, HPA* or the tick against the real types works with that worktree open — the rule that spike code is never copied into `crates/` holds either way. What survives of the spike workflows is re-expressed inside `cargo xtask ci` as the skeleton lands the corresponding checks: the three-OS hash-stream comparison (G4, G3′) becomes the determinism step's golden chains, the path-identity comparison (G2) joins it when pathing lands at S3, the geometry golden (G1) becomes the headless-screenshot check of harness part 2, and the perf budgets (G1 mesher p99, G3′ tick) arrive with the gates that set them (AGENTS.md §9 item 11). Recorded honestly: deleting now removes the in-tree reference the skeleton agents would otherwise have, and the spike workflows' hosted-runner numbers stop being refreshed; both are what the tag is for. Rejected: keeping `spikes/` until the skeleton has re-written each piece (contradicts the written lifecycle, keeps 30 000 lines of throwaway code in the product tree for months, and keeps four workflows burning runner minutes) and deleting without the tag (loses the code). Decided under the owner's standing instruction of 2026-09-14.

Option 1 **(taken)**: `getrandom = { version = "0.4", default-features = false, features = ["std"] }` in `[workspace.dependencies]`, taken by `crates/gateway` alone, and everything else in the transport hand-written over `std::net` with blocking threads — the RFC 6455 server side (the upgrade with `Host` and `Origin` checks, `Sec-WebSocket-Accept` through a SHA-1 of our own pinned to RFC 6455 §1.3's worked example and the FIPS 180-4 vectors, masked client frames required, text/close/ping/pong only, no extensions, no TLS, a frame-size cap) and JSON-RPC 2.0 over the proto crate's `Json` value and its `base64` module (item 74). *Downside:* six to nine hundred lines of protocol code the project owns on its security surface, mitigated by the loopback-only binding, the upgrade checks, the size cap and the negative tests T9's acceptance already names. *Option 2 — `tungstenite`:* less to write; *downside:* ten crates (`sha1`, `base64`, `http`, `httparse`, `rand`, `utf-8`, `bytes`, `thiserror`, `log`, `data-encoding`) on the surface v1.1 publishes, a second RNG beside the sim's own discipline, and a second base64 and JSON path beside the proto crate's. *Option 3 — no dependency at all:* not available without `unsafe`. Also recorded, no decision needed: the gateway is not a walled crate, so it reads no clock (AGENTS.md §4.5, `clippy.toml`) — time enters it as the host's tick, the rate limiter counts per tick and per window of ticks, the audit log stamps tick and sequence number, `std::time::Duration` on a socket timeout is not a clock read, and the Lull timer stays on the client side of the wall.

- **Item 101, the build-from-scratch question and the cost of finishing (raised by the owner, 2026-09-20): reuse nothing, continue as planned, no process changes.** The owner asked whether to end this implementation and restart on an open-source base, and said plainly that cost is the binding constraint: “if we dont do it cheaper, i will cancel it”. Four surveys were run before answering.
  - **Engines and voxel technology — nothing to inherit.** OpenRA is integer-deterministic by the same design as ours (`WDist`, 1024-unit angles, LUT trig) but carries documented cross-OS desyncs (issues 17899, 8863, 20089, 21903) and claims no bit-exactness; its hierarchical pathfinder is welded to `World`/`Locomotor`/traits. Recoil/Spring is floats plus `streflop` to force IEEE compliance, with macOS/ARM exactness only an unofficial fork's claim, and Lua gameplay. 0 A.D. is the closest precedent and *validates* our design — `CFixed_15_16`, integer `Sqrt`/`atan2_approx`, `ComputeStateHash`, a serialisation test — and its recurring OOS-on-rejoin bug (state that is hashed but not serialised) is exactly what AGENTS.md §4.8's three-places rule prevents. Warzone 2100 (QuickJS), Widelands (Lua inside the sync boundary), Mindustry (snapshot authority, explicitly not deterministic) and the Rust rollback crates (GGRS, bevy_ggrs, lightyear — all of which *require* a deterministic sim rather than providing one) are rejected. No mature Rust RTS exists: `oxidator` is dormant since 2023.
  - **Voxel/meshing — adopt nothing, keep `crates/mesher`.** Zylann's `godot_voxel` is alive, MIT and Godot-4.7-ready, but its mesher runs only inside Godot, which breaks the property that makes ours testable: the crate links without gdext so `cargo xtask ci`'s geometry golden and the headless CPU proxy exercise the real mesher with no engine in the loop. Adoption would retire ~2 000 lines, add 700–1 000 plus a build-and-CI redesign, lose that check and inherit a single-maintainer upstream. `block-mesh-rs`, `building-blocks` and `ndshape` are dormant; Veloren, Luanti and `bevy_voxel_world` are engines or ECS-bound. Chunk LOD is ours either way. Read `binary-greedy-meshing` (MIT, active) and Transvoxel for technique when LOD lands; do not take the dependency.
  - **Dependencies — the lever is nearly spent, but one correction was overdue.** Waves 1–3 wrote the replaceable code and pinned it with tests and goldens, so swapping in `tungstenite` (a second RNG, a second hash, and `net.rs` loses the type that makes a LAN bind inexpressible), `serde_json` (float-backed numbers, a second JSON path), `fixed`/`rand`, `pathfinding` or `rkyv` would now *add* work. `proptest` is rejected outright: it pulls `rand`, `rand_chacha` and `rand_xorshift` into the crate that defines the RNG contract (§4.7); T11 reuses `crates/verifier/tests/fuzz.rs`'s stream-seeded generator instead. Two future adoptions stand: `dot_vox` 5.2.0 at T12/T16 with `default-features = false` (its optional `ahash` must stay out of `cargo tree`), already approved; and `lexopt` 0.3.2 (MIT, zero transitive dependencies) as T15's argument parser, saving ~200 lines while keeping our exit codes and error strings ours — *option not yet taken, owner decides at T15*; the alternative `clap` generates help but adds six to ten crates and a proc-macro build, and its `--help` output becomes a golden we do not control.
  - **The gdext version pin was wrong.** `Cargo.toml`'s commented line read `godot = "0.3"`, which predates the Godot 4.7 API; gdext 0.5 is the line targeting 4.7+, current 0.5.5 (MPL-2.0, GPL-compatible, as `imbl` already is; `godot-core` pulls `glam`, which is float maths and exactly why `client-gdext` is in `WALLED_PACKAGES`). Corrected to `0.5.5` here, before T12 opens, so the lane does not spend a cycle discovering it.
  - **The cost of finishing, measured.** Wave 2 delivered ~24 agent-days for 3.38 M sub-agent tokens and wave 3 delivered 26 for 3.61 M — 141 k and 139 k tokens per agent-day, agreeing within 1.5 %, for 63 475 lines and green three-OS CI (~850 lines/agent-day, ~165 tokens/line). Of the plan's 172 agent-days, T0–T9 = 75 are merged and 97 remain: **~19 M tokens all-in (range 14–22 M) over six more runs**, the Godot lanes (T12, T16, T19 = 29 days) carrying a ×1.3–1.6 penalty for untyped GDScript against a live engine. Beyond it: **~40 M to the fun gate (30–55 M)** and **120–200 M to v1**, both speculative — S1–S3 have no task breakdown, stages are gameplay rather than scaffolding, and S2 attaches an open-ended tuning loop to a stage exit through the adversarial alarm bands.
  - **Two options were offered and declined.** *A narrowed wave* — T10 + T11 + a thin T13 + a `gamectl` printer over the event feed, ~25 agent-days and ~4 M tokens, to read a three-minute Push as text and test the premise before buying the Godot half — and *~30 % off every wave at no quality cost* (Lens B to Sonnet, since it compares the branch against a written acceptance list rather than exercising judgement; one pre-extracted context pack per lane instead of four agents each re-reading AGENTS.md, the plan and the log; reviewer file:line evidence carried into the fix prompt). **The owner declined both: “im going to have faith and proceed by allocating tokens as i have them available to spare” — wave 4 runs as planned, with the wave-3 process unchanged.** *Downside accepted, stated plainly:* the gameplay premise stays unobserved until the fun gate, which is the plan's most expensive ordering, and every wave costs ~30 % more than it needs to. Recorded so the choice is legible later, not to reopen it.
  - **Not up for reconsideration, and why:** the three-OS matrix stays — T8's template-id rule decided by `std::path::Component` passed on Windows and failed on the other two legs in that lane's first week, which is the whole bug class. Lens A stays Opus — in wave 3 it found a Scout speed slot falling off a six-slot array, a restore that trusted the file's own route digests, and a forgeable audit line. PR bodies keep their per-finding apply/reject record and their chain-re-blessing rationale, which is what makes a moved golden reviewable at all.
