Ownership and the train order t16 → t14 → t15 are item 104(2)’s and the handoff’s.
- **Item 105, the wave’s opening decisions, taken on the recommendation under the owner’s standing instruction of 2026-09-14.** **(1) T14’s `$` and `kW` rows ride as T14’s opening commits; there is no rows-first PR.** Checked against `main` before deciding: T5a’s revision 3 already carries nearly every number T14’s PLACEHOLDER line names — `economy.bmi_dollars`, `starting_bmi_multiplier`, the scaling percents, `recycle_refund_percent`, `salvage_percent`, `backlog_threshold_per_drone`, the ore yields; `power.core_surplus_kw`, `generator_output_kw` by richness, `kw_per_unit`, `revive_margin_kw`, `beacon_base_draw_kw`; `beacon.sphere_radius_voxels`, `commander.placement_range_voxels`, the locomotion costs per second, and every unit’s and structure’s cost, HP and draw — so a T5a-style PR would be close to empty. A row T14 finds genuinely missing goes in as its **first** commit (`proto/gp/v1/rules.proto`, `rules/rules.v1.json`, the regenerated tree, the revision bumped), with the new `rules_hash` recorded from that commit alone so the PR body can separate “the table moved the hash” from “behaviour moved the chain”; a number nothing in T14’s acceptance needs stays a named constant with a PLACEHOLDER (AGENTS.md §12). *Options and downsides:* rows first as their own PR (T5a’s precedent) gives the cleanest separation and lets the other two lanes start on the final `rules_hash`, but costs a fourth lane (0.4–1 M tokens under item 101’s process) to move a set that mostly exists, and the set would be guessed before the builder knows it, so a second table change would likely follow anyway; riding along (chosen, T13’s precedent) makes T14’s PR carry a `proto/**` contract change beside its hashed-state one, which the commit order and the PR body have to keep legible. **(2) The economy forecast’s response fields do not land this wave.** `GetEconomyForecastResponse` is filled by plan-core’s `$`/`kW` projection through the gateway’s knowledge handler, and neither crate’s forecast path has an owner in wave 5; fields landed now would be a shape guessed ahead of its only producer, and a proto field is forever. They land with the lane that fills them (S1’s economy work, or T19 if the wizard needs them first). *Downside:* `get_economy_forecast` keeps its documented stub through the skeleton, and the `GatewayError.Code` comment of item 103(7) stays open until the next `gp.api.v1` change, whoever makes it. **(3) `lexopt` 0.3.2 is approved for `crates/gamectl` and for no other crate** (an owner decision under AGENTS.md §3 rule 5). It has no dependencies, no proc macros and an MIT licence, and it handles what a hand-rolled parser gets wrong (`--`, combined short flags, non-UTF-8 paths on Windows). *Options and downsides:* `clap` brings a large tree, proc macros, build time and cargo-deny surface for five subcommands; a std-only parser like `xtask`’s costs nothing to approve but re-makes those edge cases in a tool whose exit codes and messages a player reads; `lexopt` generates no `--help`, so `gamectl` writes its help by hand from the one string table. T15 adds the `[workspace.dependencies]` line (root `Cargo.toml`, named in its PR body); AGENTS.md §3’s approved list gains the name in the next harness-docs PR. **(4) `xtask` is expected to need no change this wave.** Read before launch: `step_scenario` turns itself on when a `gamectl` binary with a `scenario` subcommand exists, and `step_screenshot` when `godot/project.godot` and `tests/golden/vista/expected.vista.png` exist, loading `res://scenes/vista_shot.tscn`. T15 and T16 therefore build to those names. If either finds the step cannot work as written, the change is T15’s to carry as a named contract path (the plan gives T15 the one `xtask` PR); T16 reports what it needs and the main session sequences it after T15’s, because one `xtask` change is open at a time. **(5) The first vista golden is rendered by CI’s Linux leg, not on the Windows host**, since the step compares under xvfb + lavapipe only: T16 pushes, downloads the leg’s `actual.vista.png`, looks at it, and commits it as the golden with what it shows written in the area’s README; the main session looks at it again before the merge.
- **Item 106, a hole in the plan under T16, found by checking T16’s *Needs* against `main` rather than against the plan’s wording (wave 4’s first lesson), and what the wave does about it.** **(1) What is missing.** T16 is written as if three things existed, and none does, in the plan, the log, the spec or the code: *a view feed* — no `gp.api.v1` method returns terrain voxels, dirty chunks or unit, commander and structure positions (`query_area` answers `INTERNAL`, item 103(11)), while `client-gdext` may depend on `godot`, `pharmakos-proto` and `pharmakos-mesher` only, and plan decision 17’s “the sim exposes a borrowable chunk view; client-gdext performs the conversion” presumes an edge that T12’s acceptance and item 102(3) forbid; *a host for the client* — the spec’s architecture makes the Godot client a JSON-RPC client over the loopback WebSocket and the gateway the in-process host of the sim, and nothing says which process that is or who starts it (there is no binary but `gamectl`, whose `main.rs` is a stub); *a pacing owner* — nothing outside tests calls `Host::step`, no method steps a match, and the gateway rightly reads no clock, so T16’s 2–4× speed and skip have nothing to act on. The demo of plan §1.1 needs all three (the Push is watched, the commander walks, a Generator goes up, edited voxels remesh). **(2) The wave becomes two runs, as wave 4 did.** Run 1 now: T14 and T15, which the hole does not touch. In parallel a design step writes the missing task into the plan as **T16a** (the view feed, match control and the host entry: `proto/gp/api/v1` + `crates/gateway`) and its decisions are logged as item 107 before its lane launches as run 1’s third lane. Run 2: T16, the client, after T16a merges. *Cost, said out loud:* about 8 unplanned agent-days, ≈ 1.5 M tokens at 186 k, taking the wave from 5.2 M to about 6.7 M. *Options and downsides:* launching T16 as written would have spent a 10-day lane discovering the hole and inventing a private answer inside the client, which is the expensive way to make a contract; feeding the vista from a client-side copy of the map generator (what spike G1 did) breaks the client→sim ban and the server-side fog the spec requires, and would be thrown away; deferring the view to S1 would leave the skeleton’s demo unwatchable, which is the one thing a walking skeleton is for. **(3) “The client path”, for T15’s parity acceptance, is defined now** because T15 launches now: a match hosted by the gateway’s `Host` behind a `Surface`, with each seat’s playbook arriving through `submit_plan` over a live loopback WebSocket session and sealed by `Surface::begin_push` — what `crates/gateway/tests/websocket.rs` and `two_seats_submit` already do. `gamectl scenario run` hosts through the same `Surface` and `Host` in process (the crate map gives `gamectl` no edge to the sim), and the parity test asserts its per-tick chain (`TickReport::hash`) equals the chain of that transport-driven session for the same seed, rules and playbooks. **(4) Ownership changes that follow.** `crates/gateway` beyond T14’s three named places (item 104(2)) is T16a’s, not T15’s: read before deciding, `Surface::{new, attach, open_lull, call, begin_push, step, end_recap}` and `TickReport` are already public, so `scenario run` needs no gateway change; if T15 finds otherwise it reports the exact need and stops short of editing the crate.
- **Item 107, the design of T16a, taken on the recommendation under the owner’s standing instruction of 2026-09-14, after a design step of one designer, two adversarial critics (the rules; cost and scope) and one reviser.** The section is in `skeleton-plan.md` §3; every option with its downside, T16’s amendment and the notes for T15, T17, T18, T19, T21, T22 and S7 are in `docs/design/skeleton-plan-t16a-notes.md`. **(1) Generated terrain is served whole at the skeleton; what is fogged is what changes it and what stands on it, voxel-exactly.** The design step marked this as the owner’s sentence, so it is flagged to the owner rather than buried: it is taken on the recommendation, the wire shape is identical under either answer, and switching costs about 1.5 agent-days. It adds no rule — `main` already serves the match seed to every seat as “not a secret”, the map is a pure function of seed and rules, and the estimator prices every leg as known terrain — and real terrain fog arrives with S3’s knowledge store as one mask feeding the view and the estimator. *Downsides:* the spec leans the other way (“unexplored ground”, “fogged voxels use last-known state or ×1.5 cost”); vent and seam sites are visible from round 1 (as they are to anyone who runs the generator on the public seed). *Rejected:* voxel-exact terrain fog now (+1.5 d, and the first Lull’s map is an island with the vent undrawn, because the vent is 28–44 voxels out and the core sphere is 24); chunk-granular fog (a sight rule 31 voxels wide that the spec does not state); hiding the seed (re-opens a merged T13 answer). **(2) The process model: the Godot lobby spawns a child process.** All logic is a gateway library module, `serve.rs`; the binary is `gamectl host`, about thirty lines, a named place in run 2. One config line goes in on the child’s stdin and one announce line (port, match id, admin token, the human seat’s token) comes back on its stdout pipe; the binary refuses to run with a terminal on stdout; the host exits when its stdin closes. No token touches argv, disk or a console. *Downsides:* a second process to package on two systems (T21); an internal two-line format that is not `gp.api.v1`; `session.rs` splits in two. *Rejected:* linking the gateway into the client (breaks the crate map and item 102(3)); a `[[bin]]` in the gateway (cannot link the operator at T18); a second extension (a workspace split); control over stdin (a second protocol outside scopes, limits and audit). **(3) The client paces, through four `admin` methods: `end_lull` 90, `advance_push {ms}` 91, `end_recap` 92, `report_host_clock {elapsed_ms, remaining_ms}` 93.** Game milliseconds only: no tick and no state hash ever reaches the wire (the proto’s own transport note, and a hash would hand the full state hash to the human seat’s process). Speed is how much game time the pacer asks for; skip is `advance_push {60 000}` repeated until the footer leaves `PUSH`; arguments out of range are refused, never clamped. The clock report is phase-neutral and bounded, because otherwise every token has 8 calls for a whole recap and for ever after match end — where the full-map unlock lands — and its answer carries `all_ready`, the one bit the lobby needs for “Ready ends the Lull”. *Downsides:* four forever method names only a lobby calls; match pace follows the client’s frame loop (its outcome does not, and that is tested); outside a Push the limiter’s clock is what the local lobby says it is, bounded per call. *Rejected:* the host pacing itself (a clock in a wall-guarded crate). **(4) The confinement rule changes, and says so:** no handler may step or seal, *except* the admin-scoped control handlers in `surface/control.rs`, which drive only the live match through `Surface`’s three driving methods and may name none of `Runner`, `Host`, `World`, `host_mut`, `seal_plans`, `seal_playbook`, `snapshot`, `.clone()`; `tests/confinement.rs` is rewritten to that rule and a descriptor-driven test asserts each control method needs `admin`. **(5) The view feed is one read method, `get_view` = 71 (`observe`), cursor-driven:** an empty cursor is a keyframe, any other is “what changed since”. Chunks are materials only, run-length encoded in the sim’s voxel order, one codec in `pharmakos_proto::chunk_rle`, the material table and order written into the proto comment and pinned to the sim’s by a gateway test; a chunk is in a delta iff *its bytes for that viewer* changed, so an unseen edit produces nothing at all and the unlock is just the viewer becoming unfogged. Entities are the complete visible list, built by inclusion, with opaque viewer-scoped ids (a dense row id is a count), `owner` spelt `seat.0`, whole-voxel positions, and **no** HP, power state, heading, destination, step, mandate, treasury or count. Stamps are the feed’s own `view_seq`, never a sim tick, because visibility changes in a Lull and a recap, which consume none. *Downsides:* per-viewer derived state in the gateway, rebuilt on restore (T17); full entity lists are 20–30 KB a poll at S2’s 300 units, so S2 adds an opt-in delta mode; a byte format inside `bytes` is a contract `buf breaking` cannot see. **(6) The production `Vision` is `host::SphereVision`, a labelled stopgap:** own, alive beacon spheres at `beacon.sphere_radius_voxels`, the one sight rule the spec states (“spheres give passive vision”) and the table numbers. After T14 merges, a small sim follow-up replaces it with `World::in_own_sphere` and adds Survey-lite’s sightings. `FogPolicy::eliminate` gets its first caller. **A defect on `main`, logged and not taken here:** the casual policy has no phase term, so a casual match is unfogged in the Lull too; the fix is `FogPolicy::unfogged(seat, phase)` for every fog-filtered method, at hardening or T20, because it re-blesses T13’s goldens and runs through T14’s named place. **(7) A host-side test seam, reached by no wire method:** `Host::file_voxel_edit` and `Host::file_damage`, because nothing on `main` edits a voxel or kills a seat in a hosted match and three acceptance lines need one. T16’s two hash-chain tests move to T16a, where the chain can be read in process. **(8) One committed keyframe fixture,** `tests/golden/gateway/view_keyframe/expected.keyframe.jsonl` with a readable twin, produced and drift-checked by the gateway; T16 commits a guarded byte-identical copy under `godot/fixtures/` for the hostless vista shot. No `xtask` change. **(9) Lane mechanics: 10 agent-days, one pull request by default.** The reviser recommended two (view and control, then the host loop) so T16’s vista could start earlier; the main session takes one, because a second review cycle is four more agents and token spend comes first — *downside:* T16 waits for the whole of T16a, about three lane-days of wall-clock. The seam stays as the fallback. **The rule for the one binary all three lanes regenerate:** T16a’s proto change is its first commit and alone in it; whichever lane merges later rebases, *regenerates* `crates/proto/src/generated/descriptor.binpb` and never hand-merges it, and re-blesses its schema-derived goldens with that reason. **(10) Harness-docs asks, for the wave’s harness-docs PR:** AGENTS.md §3 rule 2 naming the match host and its control handlers; the `gamectl` row gaining `host` (approved now, because run 2 needs it); the `proto` row gaining the voxel run-length codec; and the `gamectl` row’s edge to `pharmakos-operator`, which is decided at T18’s opening and not before. **(11) Seen read-only in T15’s worktree by the design step:** `gamectl` was taking a dependency on `pharmakos-sim`, because `Host::open` takes the sim’s `WorldConfig` — the gateway gives `gamectl` no way to host a match without naming a sim type. T16a therefore adds `Host::open_from(rules_json, seed, seats, settings)`; the main session moves `scenario run` onto it and removes the edge at T15’s local rebase, which the train order already puts last. **(12) Cost, said out loud.** The design step spent 0.84 M tokens over four agents against the 0.35 M the main session expected; it found three blockers the first draft would have shipped (ticks on the wire, raw ids and enemy state, acceptance lines that could not run). T16a at 10 days is about 1.9 M. The wave is now about 7.9 M against the handoff’s 5.2 M.
- **Item 108, the owner's interview on wave 5's open decisions (2026-09-21), one item at a time, each answer logged as given.** **(1) Generated terrain at the skeleton: served whole — the owner's answer, confirming item 107(1).** Every seat sees the whole generated map from the first Lull; enemy units, beacons, structures and voxel edits appear only inside own beacon spheres until the match-end unlock. *Options put and their downsides:* terrain whole (chosen) — the spec leans the other way, vent and seam sites are visible from round 1, real terrain fog waits for S3; fog terrain now — +1.5 agent-days, the first Lull's map is an island with the starting vent undrawn, protects nothing while the seed is public, S3 redefines it; fog terrain and hide the seed — re-opens a merged T13 answer and its goldens, scenario files name the seed, and the skeleton has no scouting loop to uncover ground with. The PLACEHOLDER stays: terrain fog's unit and memory are S3's, as one mask feeding the view and the estimator. **(2) The host is a child process — the owner's answer, after asking for the question to be investigated further, confirming item 107(2).** The Godot lobby spawns `gamectl host`; config goes in on its stdin, the port and tokens come back on its stdout pipe, and it exits when the game does. *What the investigation found.* Measured on this machine (Godot 4.7.2, Windows, `OS.execute_with_pipe` with `blocking = false`): the handshake round trip takes 150–190 ms, the child exits 20 ms after the pipe is closed and 0.6 s after the Godot process is hard-killed, so there is no orphan; Linux is not yet measured and is T16's to confirm in CI. From sources: Godot spawns the child with no console window and, since 4.4, inherits only the pipe handles; there is no half-close (none is needed); reads must be polled non-blocking; on Linux Godot's pipe descriptors leak into any LATER child, harmless while the lobby spawns one; Godot's macOS exporter has a `helper_executables` slot, so notarisation costs one more hardened-runtime executable; SmartScreen does not check a `CreateProcess` child, though unsigned indie executables do draw antivirus false positives; shipped precedent is Barotrauma and Don't Starve Together (recurring pain: "server failed to start"), while the in-process integrated server (Minecraft, Veloren, Luanti, Factorio, OpenTTD) is the commoner pattern. *Options put and their downsides:* child process (chosen) — one more unsigned executable for antivirus and notarisation, a "host failed to start" failure to handle, Linux pipe behaviour still to confirm; a second extension in the same process — a new workspace crate, the unfogged world in the render process's memory with compile-time separation only, and a forced choice on panics that the repo's rule (item 102(1): anything owning the sim aborts, "a sim that panicked must not keep running") makes ugly — abort closes the game window without a word, unwind leaves a dead sim to detect; child now and re-decide at T21 — throws away about a day of lobby code if it switches. `serve::run` takes any reader and writer, so the second-extension route stays additive, and a headless `gamectl host` is what v1.1's agents will want in any case. **(3) No pause control at the skeleton — the owner's answer.** The watch rig ships what the spec names: 1×, 2–4× and the instant skip to segment end. A client-paced match can be paused for free and pausing moves no hash, but the spec says "the human alone decides speed-up and skip" and never names a pause, so it is a question for the fun gate and not something a lane adds because it costs nothing. *Consequence for T16:* the pacer accumulates game time from elapsed wall time, not from frames drawn, so an unfocused or minimised window does not slow a Push beyond the pacer's backlog bound — which is also what keeps the playtest metric "Push time focused vs unfocused" meaningful. *Options put and their downsides:* no button (chosen) — a player who must step away can only skip or let it run; a pause button now — a rule the spec does not state, and a little less of "orders you cannot take back"; pause only while unfocused — erases the focused-vs-unfocused signal the fun gate wants. **(4) The main session stops and asks before run 2 — the owner's answer, against the recommendation (launch automatically).** When T16a, T14 and T15 are merged, the main session reports what landed and what it cost and waits for the owner's go before launching T16 (about 1.9 M tokens). This is a checkpoint on spend, not a change to item 101's process, and it does not re-open the declined savings. *Options put and their downsides:* launch automatically — 1.9 M committed with no checkpoint; stop and ask (chosen) — the wave idles until the owner answers and the lane caches go cold; stop, and prepare a compact first — the same, plus re-reading state afterwards. *The main session's reading, not the owner's words:* where a wave grows beyond what the owner said go to, ask before spending on the growth; T16a itself was launched without that checkpoint, under the standing instruction, and the owner was told at once. **(4, corrected by the owner the same day: “i made a mistake with answer 4. follow your recommendation and launch automatically”.)** Run 2 launches on the main session’s own word as soon as T16a, T14 and T15 are merged, under item 101’s unchanged process; the report of what run 1 landed and cost is still written, and is not a gate. The main session’s reading above — ask before spending on a wave’s growth — is withdrawn with the answer it was read from; the standing instruction of 2026-09-14 stands as it was.
- **Item 109, wave 5's run 1 merged (2026-09-22), and the decisions its three pull requests raised, taken on the recommendation under the owner’s standing instruction of 2026-09-14 and open to the owner’s overrule.** **(1) What merged.** **T16a** PR #20 (`3b067bb`): the view feed (`get_view = 71`), the four admin control methods (`end_lull 90`, `advance_push 91`, `end_recap 92`, `report_host_clock 93`), `serve::run` and `Host::open_from`, `pharmakos_proto::chunk_rle`, and the keyframe golden at `tests/golden/gateway/view_keyframe/expected.keyframe.jsonl` (288 chunks, 201 558 bytes of runs, one 256 KiB page; not cut). **T14** PR #21 (`af95103`): the economy, the grid, the mandate layer, programs and Survey-lite. **T15** PR #19 (`cbf07cf`): `gamectl` and `scenario run`. **Harness** PR #22: item 107(10)’s four AGENTS.md asks, the approved list (`getrandom`, `lexopt`), (3), (7) and (8) below, and `proto/buf.yaml`’s spent waiver deleted as its own comment instructs (T16a’s note: T16a was a proto change that discharged no held number, so the block should have gone then). **(2) How run 1 was recovered, and a rule for next time.** An API outage (529 Overloaded) on 2026-09-21 killed T14’s builder, T16a’s builder and T15’s fix pass. Both runs were resumed with a note appended only to the dead agent’s prompt (`c436cb7`). *What that got wrong:* the workflow cache replays only the unchanged **prefix** of agent calls, in call order, so the note on T14’s builder, the run’s first call, sent every later call live, including T15’s finished build and both its reviews. *Rule from now:* when one agent of a multi-lane run dies, re-run that agent alone, with its original prompt and the resume note, unless it is the first call in the run’s order. Then the previous session ended while T14’s fix pass ran its final full suite, after both fix commits and before the push. The main session finished that pass itself, because what remained was mechanical: it rebased onto T16a, fixed the one interaction (T14 added `DamageOrder::by`, and T16a’s test support builds a `DamageOrder`; `SeatId::NEUTRAL`, because the helper’s damage is nobody’s), ran the full suite, wrote the Review section from the two reviews and the fix commits, and pushed. The D: drive that holds the build targets dropped out for a while the same day; `wave-lanes.js` already takes a `build_root` argument for that. **(3) `gamectl` keeps its edge to `pharmakos-sim`.** Item 107(11) expected `Host::open_from` to remove it; it does not, because the gateway’s API is written in the sim’s types and `gamectl` names about a dozen of them (`RulesTable`, `SeatId`, `Ms`, `Tick`, `MatchSettings`, `WorldConfig`, `Plan::compile`, `EventKind`, `SeatEconomy`, `Snapshot`, `hex`). The edge is taken with `default-features = false` in rule 1’s own form, AGENTS.md’s crate map now lists it, and `gamectl` joins `xtask`’s `GUARDED_PACKAGES` and `WALL_GUARDED_PACKAGES` now instead of at T20, as T15 asked. `gamectl` drives a match only through the gateway’s `Host` and `Surface`, and its own `tests/confinement.rs` holds that. `scenario run` stays on `Host::open`: moving it to `Host::open_from` removes nothing while the edge stays. *Options put and their downsides:* keep the edge and guard it (chosen) — the CLI compiles the sim, as plan-core and the verifier already do; a re-export module in the gateway — a second public face for the sim’s types and the same compiled graph; gateway-owned wrapper types — a large duplicate API for one client. **(4) T15’s harness seal door stays as built.** `examples/playbooks/expand_east.jsonc` cannot be submitted on the skeleton map by either seat (`E0401`, `E0403`), so `expand-east-segment` plays only because the runner seals a playbook the verifier refused. Every such run prints a `note` line, and `tests/scenarios.rs` pins the door to exactly that scenario. *Options put and their downsides:* keep the door (chosen) — a harness can seal what no client could, loudly; refuse — the scenario step goes red on a committed file; change the scenario’s seats — T11’s record and T14’s re-bless both move; delete the scenario — the only scenario pinning an interpreter refusal goes with it. The door comes out when the example is re-authored for a map where it is legal, at S1. **(5) T14’s open rule questions stay PLACEHOLDERs, routed to the owner.** None is ruled here, because each belongs to the stage that tunes it; the built behaviour is the recommendation in each case. *A unit’s program comes from its kind, not its home beacon’s writ* (S1, with the mandate’s settings): gating on the writ would idle the starting mining drone, which item 90 homes to a core on Build, and leave the skeleton with no income. *The commander walks through a brownout and still draws* (S1, with the grid): parking it would make a total blackout a lockout. *An anchor dropped from a Build list strands what it paid for* (S2, with ruins). *No probe area is recorded as visited* (S3, with the reach window). *“One Generator per vent” is judged by grade and patch span* until a hashed vent table exists (S1). **(6) Deferred to T20’s harness half-week:** AGENTS.md’s status paragraphs are stale (“twelve steps”, scenarios “not in `cargo xtask ci` today”, no hash chains to compare), and are refreshed together rather than piecemeal. **(7) AGENTS.md section 4.8 gains T14’s clause:** widening the snapshot moves every verifier `report_hash` golden, because the fixture snapshot is one of that hash’s inputs. **(8) The `cargo xtask ci` job’s limit goes from 45 to 90 minutes.** `windows-latest` ran the suite in 41 minutes on PR #21 and was cancelled at 45 on PR #19, whose headless matches add several minutes; nothing failed, and macOS and Linux finished well inside it. The limit guards against a hang and is not a budget; the suite’s time budget, and which tests pay for it, are T20’s to set (a PLACEHOLDER in `ci.yml`). **(9) What run 1 cost.** Measured on the Workflow tool’s counter, the one waves 2 to 4 were measured on: T16a 1.82 M (0.72 M before the outage, 1.11 M after); T14 and T15 4.04 M (1.91 M before, about 2.13 M after, estimated from the transcripts because that run’s counter was lost when the session ended); 5.86 M in all, plus the 0.84 M design step. That is about 209 k tokens per agent-day over the plan’s 28, against wave 4’s 186 k; most of the difference is the outage, which re-ran T15’s build and reviews and paid for three agents twice.
- **Item 110, wave 5 closed (2026-09-23): run 2, T16, merged, and the decisions its pull request raised, taken on the recommendation under the owner’s standing instruction of 2026-09-14 and open to the owner’s overrule.** **(1) What merged.** **T16** PR #26 (`bd8ae2b`): `gamectl host` (the named place, naming no sim type and refusing a terminal standard output); in `crates/client-gdext` the view feed’s one decode entry (`view_apply`, `chunk_rle` through the palette, transposed, keyed by origin, the six neighbour borders T12 left unwired now wired), the pacer (`pacer.rs`, the one wall clock: elapsed time × speed owes game milliseconds, one `advance_push` in flight, the host clock reported outside a Push, the keep-alive) and the connection scheduling (`rig.rs`); in `godot/` the lobby that spawns `gamectl host` with `OS.execute_with_pipe` and holds the two tokens in variables only, the vista, the watch rig (1×, 2×, 4× and skip; no pause, item 108(3)) and the headless `watch_check` scene; and three goldens under `tests/golden/vista` (the PNG, the geometry digests, the event list). **Item 108(2) is confirmed on Linux:** the `client extension` job now runs `watch_check` against a real `gamectl host` on Windows and Linux, idles 35 s with no dropped connection, plays a segment at 4× to the recap with no caught panic, and checks that no `gamectl` outlives the client. **The vista golden** was rendered on CI’s Linux leg, looked at by the lane, and looked at again by the main session before the merge (item 105(5)): the whole generated map from above its north-east corner, one unbroken diamond with no cracks, no missing chunk and no back-face holes, as the area’s README describes; a same-runner re-render differed in 0 of 921 600 pixels. **(2) Recovery.** The session ended while the builder was waiting on its last CI run, after it had pushed all six build commits and before it opened the pull request. The builder is the run’s first call, so item 109(2)’s rule allowed the plain resume: same run id, a note on the builder only, and the reviews and fix pass ran live after it. The D: drive dropped out again; the fix pass built on C:. **(3) Contract paths accepted in the lane’s own pull request.** T16 changed `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (the `screenshot` job’s Godot install filled, the extension staged, a bootstrap render while no golden exists, an `xvfb-run` version-probe shim, `if-no-files-found` flipped to `error`, its limit 30 to 45 minutes; the `client` job’s watch run and orphan check) and `REUSE.toml` (the fixture’s annotation), and one line of `crates/gamectl/tests/confinement.rs` outside its named place (the new `host.rs` added to the files the test scans). Kept in the one pull request rather than split into a CI PR: each change is what the file itself assigned to T16 or what the brief asked for, the PR names them, and a split would have added a matrix run for nothing. *Options put and their downsides:* accept (chosen) — a lane PR that carries CI changes, against plan section 3’s standing preference for single-purpose CI PRs; split — one more PR and one more three-OS run, same content. **(4) Booked for T20’s harness half-week.** `xtask`’s `tool_available` probes a tool with `--version`, which `xvfb-run` does not have, so the screenshot step called an installed `xvfb-run` missing: probe it by path, then delete the shim. `cargo xtask screenshot` skips before rendering when no golden exists and never stages the extension: give it a render-only mode and a staging pre-step, then delete the bootstrap and staging steps from `ci.yml`. AGENTS.md: the `client-gdext` row should name the pacer, the Lull timer and the connection scheduling as the sanctioned walled exception to “it marshals; it does not decide” (the notes already rank above the row, and `tests/no_arithmetic.rs` exempts `pacer.rs` by name); a sentence should say the live gateway’s answers are not canonical proto JSON (the `_status` footer, lower-case enum values per item 80) and the client translates them; and a named-place grant should list the crate’s confinement test. These join items 102(3), 103(9), 104(6) and 109(6). **(5) Booked for the next gateway lane, beside the `SphereVision` replacement.** `serve::Config` sets no upper bound on the seat count, so `gamectl host` hosts a 99-seat match when asked; v1 allows three. Refuse seats outside 1 to 3 as `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. The lobby hard-codes two seats, so nothing reaches it today. **(6) Left for the owner at T16’s demo review, as PLACEHOLDERs in code:** the pacer period (100 ms), its backlog bound (5 000 game ms) and the speed set ({1, 2, 4}; is 3× a speed?); the keep-alive interval (5 s) and the host-clock cadence (250 ms), with `READ_TIMEOUT` at hardening; the easing, derived facing, camera and the Pall’s values; the lobby’s match settings (the golden seed, two seats, round limit 6); where a packaged client finds `gamectl`, the rules and the library (T21). Decision 22, the screenshot tolerance, is still recommended and not logged; G1’s thresholds held at 0 pixels on the first real vista. The Lull’s length is not on the wire, so the rig reads `match.lull_ms` from the client’s pinned rules copy, as the T16a notes’ section D expected. **(7) What wave 5 cost.** Run 2: about 1.54 M (0.72 M before the session ended, estimated from the transcript; 0.82 M on the Workflow counter after). Wave 5 in all: 7.40 M across 38 planned agent-days, about 195 k per agent-day, against wave 4’s 186 k; with the 0.84 M design step, 8.24 M against the 7.9 M estimate of item 106. **(8) Wave 5 is closed.** Wave 6 is next: T17 save and resume with the private replay, T18 the Easy operator and the safe playbook, T19 the editor wizard (plan section 3, row W6).
- **Item 111, wave 6's opening (2026-09-23): the holes found by checking T17, T18 and T19 against `main`, a design step, and the decisions taken for the wave, on the recommendation under the owner’s standing instruction of 2026-09-14 and open to the owner’s overrule.** **(1) What was found.** Checking each task’s *Needs* against `main` rather than against the plan’s wording (item 106’s lesson) found that none of the three is buildable as written. No wire path carries the operator’s suggestion or a “why” to the wizard, templates declare no parameters, and `render_plan` answers one prose string, so a chip has nothing to hang on (H1). The operator’s only seam, `serve::BuiltInSeat`, takes the gateway’s own `Request`, and the “gp.api.v1 service traits” AGENTS.md section 3 names do not exist (H2). The safe playbook filed on a miss is one constant per host, not the seat’s own (H3). T17’s save lives in the gateway, which has no restore path, and sealed playbooks are not on disk at all: `MatchCache::seat_directory` has no caller, so notebooks, drafts and seals live only in memory (H4). The design step found eight more: a built-in seat cannot finish a round under the rate limit, because a Lull’s tick moves only on a clock report (H8); nothing a client can call returns `$` or `kW`, so neither the operator nor the demo’s meter can read them (H9, H10); `Setup.built_in` is sized before the config line is read (H11); the operator’s tuning rows are on no wire (H12); the constant is not the spec’s safe playbook (H13); a new `BeaconSummary` field breaks the Godot unit’s test literals (H14); an advisor’s `get_view` writes into the human’s per-viewer feed (H15); and the cache cannot resume (H16). Item 84 had already answered plan decision 13 (build save and resume); it does not mention the private replay, which rides T17’s plan line only. **(2) The design step.** One designer, two adversarial critics (the rules; buildability, cost and scope) and one reviser, as item 107’s, for 0.90 M tokens. Its result, `docs/design/skeleton-plan-w6-notes.md`, is adopted without change: where it and plan section 3’s T17, T18 and T19 lines disagree, it wins. The plan gains a `### T18a` section (the notes’ A1) and an amendment line under each of the three. **(3) The decisions** (the notes’ section C gives every option and its downside). C1: a template declares its parameters in `gp.v1.Meta.parameters = 6` (pointer and label, untyped until S6). C2: `instantiate_template` gains `suggested` and answers the filled parameters and a “why”, computed by an advisor at each Lull’s start for every seat with no built-in operator. C3: chips move to S3; the rule list is `render_plan`’s prose lines. C4: the operator depends on `pharmakos-proto` alone and drives a call closure that `gamectl host` adapts, so rule 3 becomes a dependency fact. C5: each seat’s safe playbook is the operator’s, filed after its own FULL verify with the constant as the audited fallback, and `get_safe_plan` answers the seat’s own. C6: in-process tokens get their own rate limit, and Easy’s call budget is derived from its evaluation units. C7: `GetEconomyForecastResponse` 1–4 as present-state values, and `BeaconSummary`’s owner plus own-only core, priority and powered — **a departure from item 105(2), taken in the open**, because the safe playbook cannot tell that power is short without them and the demo row promises a meter. C8: saves are automatic at item 84’s Lull boundaries (at `begin_push`, and on control end-of-file in a Lull), one slot per match, and a sealed save resumes into its Push. C9: resume is the config line’s seventh field. C10: a gateway-owned JSON save container; `SNAPSHOT_VERSION` does not move. C11: the private replay is inputs only (sealed files, per-segment hash files), its log a PLACEHOLDER for S7. C12: `World::in_own_sphere`, as items 107(6) and 110(5) name it. C13: a flat `library/` at the repository root, MIT OR Apache-2.0. C14: two runs. C15: no random draw at Easy. C16: the safe template is the spec’s, the constant becomes its nothing-raised form, and `deploy-and-visit`’s chain moves once, in T18a, for that stated reason. C17: the operator reads the public rules text for its tuning rows. **(4) Five owner questions, taken on the recommendation and flagged here so they are not buried** (the notes’ section D, “for the owner now”). An in-process seat gets its own rate limit (the alternative, a resumable operator, costs about 1.5 d). A save made at a Push’s start resumes into that Push (the alternative lets a player take back sealed orders by killing the client). The advisor holds a `plan`-scoped in-process token on the human’s seat, never `plan.submit`, behind a method allow-list (the alternative, no advisor for the human, saves about 2 d and loses the spec’s pre-fill). Scouts and sightings stay out of the live view, as item 108(1) says, although item 107(6) read otherwise. Saving is automatic where the spec says the host “can” save. Each changes a lane’s brief if overruled; the first and third touch run 1. **(5) The lane plan.** Before run 1 the main session lands a struct-update base on the two `BeaconSummary` literals in `crates/client-gdext/tests/fixtures.rs` (H14, in this item’s pull request). Run 1: T18a (`proto/**`, plan-core, the gateway, `library/`, `gamectl host.rs`’s library path; a contract PR) and T19 PR 1 (the Godot unit), merged t19a then t18a. Between the runs: T18a merged, then a harness-docs PR (the operator row, the `gamectl` → operator edge, rule 3’s sentence on in-process rates, rule 2’s `file_advice`, `library/`’s licence, `buf.yaml`’s ignore block deleted) and the item recording run 1. Run 2, launched automatically after (item 108(4)): T17 (sim and gateway; a contract PR), T18 (operator and `gamectl`’s named place), T19 PR 2, merged t17, t18, t19b, with `library/` frozen. **(6) Cost.** 34.75 agent-days against the plan’s 22 (T18a 8.75, T19 PR 1 5.5, T17 6, T18 8, T19 PR 2 6.5): about 6.8 M tokens at wave 5’s 195 k per agent-day, 7.5–8.2 M if the Godot lanes run dear, plus this step’s 0.90 M. The plan’s total moves from 182 to about 194.75 agent-days. Five cuts, in order, would bring the wave to about 30.25 d (5.9 M): no advisor for the human (−2 d), defer the replay (−0.75), operator-defined parameters (−0.75), the meter to S1 (−0.5), Resume to T22 (−0.5). None is taken; the estimate is reported, not a gate (item 108(4)). **(7) Housekeeping.** `wave-lanes.js` now asks lane commits for the model that runs the lanes, Opus 5.5, where it named an older one, and its header shows the `scriptPath` form it is launched with. Item 93’s “item 80” for the three templates means item 81 (item 80 is the JSON-RPC casing).
- **Item 112, wave 6’s run 1 merged (2026-09-24), and the decisions its two pull requests raised, taken on the recommendation under the owner’s standing instruction of 2026-09-14 and open to the owner’s overrule.** **(1) What merged.** **T19 PR 1**, PR #30 (`1590aae`): the editor’s map route surface (beacon and ground actions, the Alt-click selector, routes drawn from `estimate_route` legs with each leg’s time as the gateway gives it), the per-click legality ghost from a QUICK verdict, the validation rows with Fix, Load’s refusal with a code and a pointer, the notes box, draft continuity, submit and Ready, and a headless run of all of it against a real `gamectl host` on both legs. **T18a**, PR #29 (`840f150`): the planning wire — `gp.v1.Meta.parameters`, `instantiate_template{suggested}` with its filled parameters and “why”, the advisor seam behind `serve::Operators` with its method allow-list and its own rate, each seat’s own safe playbook with the constant as the audited fallback, the own-economy and own-beacon fields, and the three templates in `library/`. Its contract paths, accepted in the lane PR as item 110(3) did for T16: `proto/**`, `proto/buf.yaml`’s ignore block, `REUSE.toml` and a new `library/LICENSE`. As item 111 expected, `deploy-and-visit`’s chain moved once (from tick 1, because the fallback safe playbook became spec section 14’s), and no determinism or `report_hash` golden moved. Three departures from the brief, each stated in its PR: `FilledParameter` holds 5–15 for the typed catalogue (additive); the safe template’s raise parameter is the whole route (`/declarative/route`, replaced with `[to_safety, raise…]`), because a JSON Pointer cannot name steps that exist only when raised; and an advisor’s `get_view` is answered from a throwaway clone of the view feed, so the human’s feed is untouched and the operator keeps its view. The gateway’s walkthrough golden records summaries rather than fields, so new fields do not move it; a field’s shape needs its own test. **(2) Recovery, and a rule for next time.** The machine went down while both fix passes ran, and the D: drive that holds the build targets disappeared with it. The builds and all four reviews had finished. `wave-lanes.js` puts the build directory in every prompt, so resuming the run on C: would have re-run every agent. The main session generated a fix-only workflow from `wave-lanes.js` instead, with each lane’s build report and findings written into it and a note saying what the dead pass had left, and ran the two fix passes alone. *Rule from now:* when a dead run can resume unchanged, resume it (item 109(2)); when the build directory must change, re-run only the dead agents from a generated script. **(3) What T19 PR 1 found for other lanes, and where each goes.** A commented file with an out-of-vocabulary construct gets E0001 at `/byte/0` instead of the construct’s code and pointer, because `verify_jsonc` hands raw text to a verifier that cannot read comments: T17, with that one function in `crates/plan-core` as a named place. `estimate_route` writes `Leg.to` as a bare voxel where `gp.api.v1.Leg.to` is a `gp.v1.Location`: T17, pinned by its own test because the walkthrough would not see it. A stale `carried` draft outlives its round when nothing new is carried: T17. No method returns a draft’s body, so a restarted client cannot open last round’s draft: (4). The wire carries no rounded travel time (item 57: “a short route’s ETA rounded generously or shown in whole seconds”), and the editor shows raw game milliseconds rather than do time maths: a PLACEHOLDER in code, owner, S3. The lobby’s Ready cannot end a two-seat Lull until a built-in seat calls `set_ready`: T18. Aiming an Attack beacon at a known enemy beacon is S2’s. **(4) “The editor’s bytes equal plan-core’s canonical bytes” is read as “equal to plan-core’s own output for the same inputs”** (`patch_text` for an edit, `instantiate_template` for the wizard). It cannot hold literally: `patch_plan` keeps the file’s layout and writes an inserted value compactly, and no method returns canonical text. T19 PR 1 asserts the reading live on both legs, and T19 PR 2 is held to it. *Options put and their downsides:* this reading (chosen) — an edited file is never canonical on disk; canonical insertion in `patch_plan` and `instantiate_template` — plan-core work, and every patched file’s layout moves; a canonicalising method — one more forever method. The owner decides at S3, with the authoring stage. **(5) `get_draft` = 57, in T17** — an addition to spec section 12’s method list, and a departure from the notes’ section B, which kept `proto/**` out of run 2: T17’s contract PR now also carries `gp.api.v1` and a regenerated descriptor, and T18 rebases over them. `GetDraftRequest {draft_id}` answers `{playbook_jsonc, label, round}`, `SCOPE_PLAN`, in the Planning group, for the caller’s own drafts only, `NOT_FOUND` for any other id, and it is not on the advisor’s allow-list. Spec section 13 opens every Lull with last round’s playbook as an editable draft, and after a resume the client is a new process with no copy of it. *Options put and their downsides:* the method (chosen) — one more forever method; the body on `DraftSummary` — every `list_drafts` carries up to 32 whole playbooks, and it is a proto change too; the client keeps its own copy — a second copy of a playbook outside the private match cache, gone after a crash and wrong after a round the gateway filed; defer — draft continuity breaks on every restart, which a resume always is. **(6) T19 PR 2 becomes run 3, after T17 and T18 merge** — a departure from item 111(5), and it overrides the notes’ A4 items 2 and 3: PR 2 runs in run 3 and needs T17 and T18 merged. It calls three things those lanes add: `get_draft` and the resume line (T17) and the real operator’s suggestions (T18). `library/` stays frozen until PR 2 merges, because PR 2 copies the `instantiate_suggested` golden, which embeds a template. *Options put and their downsides:* run 3 (chosen) — about one run of wall-clock time and one idle slot in run 2, no tokens; PR 2 in run 2 against a fixture copy and a live check that skips while the host lacks resume — both turn on for the first time in CI after a rebase; PR 2 in run 2 without Resume and restart continuity, which follow in a run-3 PR — two PRs and two review cycles; Resume to T22, item 111(6)’s cut — the demo’s resume line waits. *Interim state, known and accepted:* between T17’s merge and PR 2’s, saves are automatic and a reused match id is refused, while the lobby still names a match `local-<pid>`; a local run that reuses a process id meets the refusal until PR 2 gives the lobby a unique id. **(7) The harness-docs changes, in this item’s own pull request.** AGENTS.md: the operator row (its library depends on `pharmakos-proto` alone and reaches the match through a closure the gateway binds to the seat’s own in-process token and `gamectl` adapts to `serve::Operators`; the “`gp.api.v1` service traits” never existed), the `gamectl` row’s edge to `pharmakos-operator`, rule 2’s in-process seats, rule 3’s in-process door, rate and notebook read, and section 8’s licence row for `library/`; `proto/buf.yaml`’s ignore block deleted and its rule’s comment restored. Two of item 110(4)’s AGENTS.md items are pulled forward from T20, overriding the notes’ section B line that kept them there, because the editor and operator lanes lean on them: rule 4 names the pieces that schedule or draw without deciding (the pacer’s clock, the Lull’s countdown and the FULL idle timer, `rig.rs`’s scheduling and its `end_lull`, the route-target reader, the `owner`-based map menu), and says every client of the gateway’s JSON-RPC answers translates them because they are not canonical proto JSON. *Downside:* a second AGENTS.md edit before T20’s refresh. Item 110(4)’s third AGENTS.md item (a named-place grant listing its confinement test), its `xtask` items and the status paragraphs (item 109(6)) stay T20’s. **(8) Run 2’s briefs were reviewed before launch** by three adversarial agents (the AGENTS.md text against the code; this item against the PR bodies; the briefs against the notes), whose findings are applied here and in the briefs: T18’s hosted-match tests live in `crates/gamectl/tests`; Easy’s evaluation units and thresholds are named constants with PLACEHOLDERs, since the rules table has no rows for them; T17 keeps every public item `gamectl` names source-compatible; tests that host a match use a match id unique to each run, since a save now outlives its process; a resume line must match all six of the save’s fields. **(9) What run 1 cost.** About 2.9 M on the Workflow counter’s scale. The first run’s counter was lost with the session; its transcripts sum to 3.15 M by the final-context-plus-output formula, which over-read the two runs whose counters survived (the fix re-run, 0.26 M measured against 0.29 M; the design step, 0.90 M against 1.15 M) by 13 and 27 per cent, so about 2.6 M, plus the fix re-run’s 0.26 M. Item 111 estimated 2.8 M for run 1’s 14.25 agent-days at wave 5’s 195 k per agent-day; the result is about 200 k.
- **Item 113, wave 6’s run 2 merged (2026-09-25), and the decisions its two pull requests raised, taken on the recommendation under the owner’s standing instruction of 2026-09-14 and open to the owner’s overrule.** **(1) What merged.** **T17**, PR #32 (`5e13d1b`…`523e043`): saves at item 84’s two Lull boundaries, one `save.json` per match; resume as the config line’s seventh field, refused as `INVALID_ARGUMENT` unless the six saved values and the rules, verifier and snapshot stamps all match; `Host::resume` as the one restore, a `sealed` save resuming into its Push and a `lull` save into its Lull; a new match refused over a saved one; the private replay as inputs only; `World::in_own_sphere` under `SphereVision`; seat counts outside 1–3 refused; and item 112’s four additions for it (`get_draft = 57`, `Leg.to` as a `gp.v1.Location`, the stale carried draft dropped, comments blanked before the verifier reads a non-canonical file). Contract paths, accepted in the lane PR as item 112(1) did for T18a: `get_draft = 57` alone in its commit with the descriptor regenerated; the save container and the replay files ((12)); a new sim query beside the determinism code, `World::spheres` and `World::in_own_sphere` (`crates/sim/src/sight.rs:118`, `:159`), read-only, so no hashed state moved; the config line’s optional seventh field, with an eighth refused; and doc comments in `snapshot.rs` and `interpreter/state.rs`. `SNAPSHOT_VERSION` did not move, and the one golden that moved is `tests/golden/proto/expected.method-scopes.txt`. Accepted as built: a `sealed` resume is sealed through `begin_push`’s own body, so orders enter a match by one path; audit sequence numbers and the gateway’s tick carry on across a resume; a resumed view’s identity folds in the audit log’s last sequence number, so the dead process’s cursors are stale; and `serve::run_in` takes a data root, which every gateway hosting test now uses (T18’s `crates/gamectl/tests/operator_host.rs` hosts through `serve::run` in the real per-user cache instead, under a run-unique id, `:221`, `:411-435`). Eleven review findings (two majors: test data roots shared between processes, and a resumed view minting the dead process’s view id), all applied. **T18**, PR #33 (`8ca20ec`…`6dd8e9c`, merged as rebased commits whose tree is the pre-merge head `b7c7f23`’s (the reviewed commits plus the main session’s REUSE commit, (10)), so the rebase moved no golden, `tests/golden/operator` included): the operator on `pharmakos-proto` alone; Easy over a call closure, ending every round with `set_ready`; each seat’s safe playbook instantiated from the library template; `EASY_CALL_BUDGET` (68) and the advisor’s 55 as `const` expressions over the evaluation units; `gamectl host`’s `EasyOperators` playing every seat but the human’s and advising the human’s; six operator goldens. Corpus: 23 rows, 7 of them Easy’s own plan (7/7, no repair) and 16 its safe playbook. Baseline, not a gate: about 10 ms of the surface thread per in-process seat per Lull (20.0–56.0 ms for two or three seats), against P2’s 200 ms, which stays S5’s. Contract paths: one row in `tests/golden/README.md`, the root `Cargo.toml`’s uncommented entry, and (10)’s `REUSE.toml` block. Twenty review findings in 18 rows (one major: the raised safe playbook had never met the real verifier, now a test), none rejected, one raised for the owner ((10)). **(2) The run died and resumed from its own cache.** The app stopped at 00:05 on 2026-09-25, after both builds and two of the four reviews. No prompt had to change, so the same run id was resumed from its baked script: the four finished agents replayed from the cache and only the rest ran live. That is item 112(2)’s rule (“when a dead run can resume unchanged, resume it”), confirmed; nothing is added to it. **(3) Two harness lessons, fixed in `wave-lanes.js` in this item’s pull request.** Cancelling its own suite, T18’s builder force-stopped every `cargo`, `rustc` and `xtask` process on the machine (its finding 9). That probably explains T17’s full suite stopping with cargo exiting −1 in `crates/gamectl/tests/parity.rs` and no failing test: T17 found no cause in the code and T18 says only that T17’s run may have been cut short, and no timestamps were compared. The two lanes also shared one scratch folder, so T18’s scripts overwrote T17’s generically named ones (`fix4.py` among them) mid-pass. `wave-lanes.js` now tells every agent never to stop a process it did not start (nothing by image name; its own run only by the PID it launched), and gives each agent `<scratch>/<lane-id>/<agent>/` for scripts, notes and probes (a lane’s two reviews run at once), while the PR bodies and CI logs keep their lane-prefixed names in the parent. *Options put and their downsides:* the prompt rule (chosen) — nothing enforces it; one full suite at a time — wall-clock in every run; isolating each lane’s processes — nothing a workflow script can reach. A folder per lane (chosen) — two conventions in one parent; moving the PR bodies and logs as well — changes paths that the fix prompt and item 112(2)’s generated script read. **(4) T18 finding 1: the safe playbook’s raise can never fire.** As built (`crates/operator/src/safe.rs:123-134`, from the notes’ A3 item 2, a PLACEHOLDER), “short” is own `headroom_kw_now < 0` and “at risk” is an own non-core beacon with `powered = false`, and the two never hold on one snapshot: every snapshot after the first follows a settle, and `brown_out` sheds until supply covers draw (`crates/sim/src/power.rs:455-489`), so headroom below zero exists only on map generation’s tick-0 columns ((5)), where no seat has a non-core beacon yet. The scripted test pins the real post-shed state as “nothing raised” (`crates/operator/tests/scripted.rs:753-768`), and the hosted test forces both answers (`crates/gamectl/tests/operator.rs:346`). Spec section 14 defines neither word. *Options put and their downsides:* as built — dead in hosted play, at S1 and S2 as well; “short” as any own beacon browned out, or headroom below zero (the builder’s) — a raise does not relight a dark beacon (`power.rs:456-458`, `:551`), it only orders the next revival and shed, and the same beacon is raised again at every timeout; **that reading, skipping beacons already HIGH** (chosen) — the same, less the repeat, for one more field (`priority`, on the wire at `crates/gateway/src/surface/knowledge.rs:589-599` and unread by `crates/operator/src/situation.rs:31-44`); the lit beacons next in the brownout order, as T18a’s proto comment reads (`proto/gp/api/v1/gateway.proto:608-614`) — restates `power.rs:491-526` in the operator, and drifts at S1; a threshold at the revive margin — fires on a busy seat at 0 kW, and invents a number; demand on the wire — a permanent field before S1’s review (item 105(2)) and a contract PR; defer — the spec’s sentence stays unimplemented and the scripted test keeps asserting the wrong reading. The safe playbook’s “why” follows the same reading, since today it keys on the headroom alone (`crates/operator/src/compose.rs:343-360`) and would tell a seat with a dark beacon out of reach that power is not short; with nothing dark it stays byte-identical. - **Item 115, the pace review of 2026-09-26 and its adjustments.** The owner asked whether the plan is working or needs adjusting from lessons learned, hoping the work had accelerated, and then said “execute your adjustments”; taken on the recommendation, and (7)’s question put to the owner. Times are UTC. **(1) Where the skeleton stands.** About 180 of its roughly 201 agent-days are merged, 12 calendar days after its first pull request (#1, 2026-09-15), about five of them a pause (from 2026-09-16 until wave 4 launched late on 09-20); the plan’s schedule (section 4’s table) put the skeleton’s end at week 14.2. Run 4 (T18b) is building; W7 (T20, T21) and W8 (T22) remain, then the owner’s stage demo. **(2) Pace: the runs have slowed, not sped up, and most of the slowing is stops.** *Per run*, from launch to its last merge: wave 3 about 4.5 h; wave 4’s three runs about 3.1, 4.8 and 2.8 h; wave 5’s two about 28.8 h (the 529 outage, then 19 h after the session ended as both workflows finished) and 20.4 h (a 16 h stop: the session ended during the build and killed its builder before it opened its pull request); wave 6’s runs 1 to 3 about 22.6 h (the machine went down and D: vanished during the fix passes, 17.5 h), 23.7 h (the app stopped overnight and about 18 h passed before the run resumed from its own cache) and 13.0 h. Run 3 stopped too, for about 6 h: its last CI run went green at 09:33 (run 36229658078), `fix:t19b` took no further step until 12:23, when it and the main session both stopped on the account’s weekly limit, and the session went on only at the owner’s “Try again” at 15:29. Its other 7 h went: 5.9 h from launch to the last green check — builds 1.5 and 2.1 h, reviews 0.1 to 1.5 h, fix passes 2.4 h each to green, each of which pushes and then watches a Windows leg of 68 to 70 min, against wave 4’s fix passes of 0.9 to 2.0 h over an 18-to-34-min leg (#14 to #18) — and 1.1 h for the second lane’s rebase and a second full matrix. Without its stops, run 3 took one and a half to two and a half times as long as wave 4’s runs. *Per wave*, from the first launch to the last merge: wave 5 merged its 38 planned agent-days in about 49 h, roughly 18.5 a day, and wave 6 its 36.25 so far in about 62 h, roughly 14 a day. Wave 6 needed four serial runs instead of the two item 111 planned: item 112 (6) moved T19 PR 2 behind T17 and T18 into a third run; holes found mid-wave became two unplanned lanes, T14b and T18b (item 113); and T18b had to follow T14b, because T14b moves every chain from the first settle and no two lanes that touch `crates/operator` run side by side (item 113 (14)). Run 3 paired a 1.5-day lane with a 6.5-day one, and run 4 had one lane until T20a joined it. *Between runs*, each launch waited 50, 68 and 97 min (72 on average) for the docs pull request recording the previous run (#31, #34, #37) to pass the three-OS matrix and merge. *Cost* per planned agent-day has crept from 186 k (wave 4) and 195 k (wave 5) to 215 k and 245 k (wave 6’s runs 2 and 3), and wave 6’s design and review passes cost about 6 M besides: 0.90 M, 0.58 M, 2.62 M, 0.48 M and 1.18 M on the Workflow counter (item 111’s design step, the review of the between-runs docs, item 113’s design pass, the review of item 113’s docs, and item 114’s review), and 0.27 M for one agent’s coherence check of the run-4 brief. **So the levers are the stops — the session, the app or the machine going down, or the usage limit — which took about 76 of the 108 h of wave 5’s and wave 6’s five runs (19, 16, 17.5, 18 and 6 h); the CI leg, which grew from 18–34 min in wave 4 to 68–70 and which every run pays at least twice in series; and the serial wait for docs pull requests.** A workflow’s end was not one: in every run whose session was up when its workflow ended, the merge train started within three minutes. The stops are outside the lanes, and the largest single lever is the owner’s: a run finishes in hours only while the app, the session and the machine stay up and the plan’s usage limits have room. **(3) Adjustment: a run launches as soon as its docs pull request and lane briefs pass review.** The docs pull request that records the previous run and opens the next merges beside the run instead of before it. *Options and their downsides:* keep gating the launch on the docs pull request — about an hour idle at every boundary until (4) lands, minutes after it for a prose-only docs pull request; copy the new item’s text into the lane’s `extras` — the lane then reads a copy that can drift from the reviewed docs; **launch at once, with `wave-lanes.js`’s new `docs_ref` argument naming the docs pull request’s branch** (chosen): every agent copies each file that branch adds or changes under `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` and `docs/design/` and reads the copy in place of its worktree’s, and reads `origin/main` once the branch is gone. Until the docs pull request merges, the lane reads text not yet on `main`, which is safe only because the docs are reviewed before the launch; if a late review changes them, the main session tells the run or re-runs the agents concerned. This holds only for a docs pull request that touches nothing but `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/**` and `.claude/**`, which no skeleton lane has edited (the brief’s rule (e) forbids `AGENTS.md`, and `docs_ref`’s note forbids committing `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` and `docs/`). One that carries anything else — a base the lanes build on, as item 111’s did (`crates/client-gdext/tests/fixtures.rs`), or `REUSE.toml`, a licence file or a `tests/golden` README, as item 113’s did — still merges before the launch. The docs pull request merges on its own as soon as it is green, never at the head of the lanes’ train, because the train rebases and re-runs whatever follows a merge (`scripts/merge-train.sh:114-117`) and the ruleset does not require a lane to be up to date. `docs_ref` is in every agent’s prompt, so a resume keeps it unchanged even after the docs pull request has merged: a changed value re-runs every agent that had finished, as item 112 found for the build directory. **(4) Adjustment: a docs-only fast path in CI.** A pull request that touches only prose should not wait about 68 min for three `cargo xtask ci` legs. *Options and their downsides:* a `paths-ignore` filter on `ci.yml` — the ruleset’s eight required checks never report on such a pull request, so it can never merge; a job-level `if:` that can be false — a skipped matrix job reports under its unexpanded name, so the five required matrix checks (three `cargo xtask ci`, two `client extension`) never report, and only the three single jobs would report their skip as success; **every required job runs as today, and each that builds decides after its checkout whether anything but prose changed** (chosen). The decision reads every path the pull request adds, modifies, deletes or renames, both sides of a rename included, from the checked-out merge commit against its first parent, and treats a path as prose only if it is on an allow-list: `docs/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/**` and top-level `*.md`. When only prose changed, the `DCO sign-off` job runs as today, the ubuntu `cargo xtask ci` leg runs the suite’s `reuse` step alone, every other required job skips its remaining steps, `if: always()` uploads included, and reports success, and the cross-OS guard takes the legs’ answer, including once its FLIP AT G4 lines flip. Any event but `pull_request` (a push to `main`, `workflow_dispatch`) runs everything, any error in the decision runs everything, and nothing can force the fast path. Its downsides: each job still costs a runner start, and a path wrongly counted as prose skips the suite, which is why the list allows rather than denies and the decision is an `xtask` command with unit tests. `scripts/merge-train.sh` needs no change: a fast-path job concludes success, which `gh pr checks` lists as `pass` (`:51-56`). It changes what a green `cargo xtask ci (…)` check means, so each fast-path job says so in a `::notice::`, and the pull request that records its merge adds a sentence to AGENTS.md section 9 and CLAUDE.md’s Commands paragraph saying that a prose-only pull request runs the DCO walk and the `reuse` step in place of the suite (the main session’s, since lanes do not edit either file). For such a pull request, item 86’s gate “`cargo xtask ci` on the branch” becomes the DCO walk and the `reuse` step, with the full suite on `main`’s push. That is taken on the recommendation, unlike (7), because a change confined to the allow-list cannot change what the suite checks; the owner can overrule it. **(5) Adjustment: T20a, beside T18b in run 4.** The CI leg is the lever in (2) that the lanes control, and item 113 (9) had already chosen its first cut: narrow `test-research` to `pharmakos-sim`, the one crate whose code the `research` feature changes. On #37’s run 36258107115 the part of `test-research` that the narrowing removes took 18.7 min on Windows, 17.9 on Linux and 16.9 on macOS (item 113 (9) measured about 13 on T18), so the Windows leg should drop from about 68 min to about 49. Clippy’s research pass still compiles every crate against a research sim (`xtask/src/main.rs:762-779`). *Options and their downsides:* leave both in T20, in W7 — run 4’s own merges and W7’s runs pay the long leg; **split them out as T20a, a 1.5-agent-day lane owning `xtask` and `.github/workflows/**`, launched now beside T18b, which touches neither** (chosen) — the one-xtask-pull-request rule then binds T20 to wait for T20a’s merge, and the narrowing is a contract change to `ci` and to AGENTS.md section 9 item 5 (the main session’s sentence, as in (4)); the other crates’ tests stop running against a research sim they never ship with, the downside item 113 (9) named. T20a also carries item 114 (5)’s stale watch-check step comment (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:615-622`). The plan gains `### T20a`; T20 keeps the rest of its unit, and the `[profile.*]` question only if the leg is still near its limit. T18b and T20a are separate workflows, so each merges by its own train; before the second merges, the main session rebases it onto `main` and waits for its matrix on the combination, as item 85 requires. **(6) Kept: no idle time after a workflow ends.** When a run’s workflow ends, the main session reads each pull request (item 114’s rule) and starts the merge train at once, as it already did in every run whose session was up. Run 3’s 3.1 h after its workflow were the weekly limit, which this does not touch. **(7) Put to the owner, not taken: the second lane of a train.** The train rebases each later lane and waits for a full three-OS matrix again (1.1 h in run 3). The option is that the main session runs the full `cargo xtask ci` locally on the rebased branch (about 15 to 25 min on a warm target) and merges when that and the pre-rebase three-OS matrix are green, with `main`’s own push run as the three-OS check of the combination. Its downsides: a cross-OS difference that only the combination shows is caught after the merge, and `main` can be red until it is reverted; and it relaxes item 85’s condition (“once CI is green on the branch”; CLAUDE.md’s paraphrase, “once `cargo xtask ci` is green on the branch”, could be read as met by a local run, which is one more reason it is the owner’s). **(8) Kept.** The pre-launch adversarial review of the docs pull request and every lane brief (item 114’s found five majors, one of them a test premise T14b had made false), item 101’s review count, no two `crates/operator` lanes side by side, and item 113 (14)’s reasons for not running T21 beside T18b. **(9) Watched.** The Windows leg ran 68 to 70 min on run 3’s pull requests (after 61 to 69 on run 2’s, item 113 (9)) against its 90-min limit, and T18b adds two hosted matches. **(10)** Run 4’s close is item 116.

In an export `ProjectSettings.globalize_path("res://")` is empty, so today’s root fallback in `godot/scripts/host_link.gd` gives `""` (the probe); in an exported build (`OS.has_feature("template")`) it becomes the executable’s folder, and it stays as it is in the editor and in a `--path` run; `find_gamectl` already looks beside the executable. `gamectl`’s default root stays the working directory, so `gamectl seat doctor` passes when run from the extracted folder (all six checks, the probe) and fails three of six from anywhere else without `--root`, which the note says. The client keeps its inline rules copy (`godot/scripts/mesher_rules.gd`, pinned by `the_inline_rules_table_is_the_committed_one`); the host reads `rules/` beside `gamectl`. **The idle lobby crashes in an export, and T21 fixes it:** the lobby’s `_process` pumps `host_link.gd` every frame, and before New match `_read_announce` calls `get_buffer` on a null `_stdio`; the editor’s debug VM logs a SCRIPT ERROR each frame and carries on, which is why CI never saw it, and the release template segfaults on the lobby’s second frame (the probe: `--quit-after 2` exits 139; a one-line guard makes it exit 0). rules and templates compiled into `gamectl` (contradicts the spec’s local-folder library and T13’s PLACEHOLDER). **(4) Item 102 (1)’s client profile.** `[profile.release-client]` inherits `release` with `panic = "unwind"` and is used by `cargo xtask package` for the client library alone; The ruleset is not changed (the owner’s); because `scripts/merge-train.sh` stops on any check that is not pass or skipping, a red package blocks a merge anyway. *Downsides:* four more jobs’ minutes on every pull request, beside the Windows leg (the lane measures whether they lengthen the critical path), and pressure on an Actions cache already over its 10 GB (LRU eviction); the zips of a public repository’s runs can be downloaded by any signed-in GitHub user for their retention, a smaller exposure than a release, which the owner accepts or narrows; `--local-verify`’s `MATRIX_ONLY` does not yet send `library/`, `rules/`, `packaging/`, `LICENSES/`, `REUSE.toml` or `tests/golden/package/` to the matrix, which T21 proposes. *Rejected:* packaging only on `main`’s push and tags (a broken zip found after the merge). **(9) The zip writer.** std-only, in `xtask`: stored entries (no compression), CRC-32, Unix mode 0755 on the game executable, `gamectl` and every directory entry, and 0644 on the other files (so a tester’s `unzip` keeps both runnable and every folder enterable), sorted entries and a fixed timestamp, so a zip’s bytes depend only on its files, and a reader of its own central directory for the manifest. *Downside:* a larger download than a deflated zip (the lane records the size); compression is a PLACEHOLDER for hardening. *Rejected:* `7z`, `zip` or `tar` (a different tool per runner, and mode bits that depend on it). **(10) The manifest golden.** `tests/golden/package/`, one list per platform (`expected.windows.txt`, `expected.linux.txt`): every entry of the zip, sorted, LF, read back from its own central directory; `package` joins `SELF_COMPARED_AREAS` and the package job compares it; the area gets its README. Because Dependabot writes the body, and `@dependabot recreate` overwrites any edit to it, the main session names the contract paths touched, and the head commit the reviews read, in a comment on the pull request before it merges; that takes the place of CLAUDE.md’s “a PR whose body names the contract paths it touches”, since item 85 asks only that the paths be named and the rebase merge carries neither body nor comment into `main`’s history. The merge is `gh pr merge --rebase --match-head-commit` on that head, not `scripts/merge-train.sh`, which rebases and force-pushes a lane’s branch from its worktree (every pair after a run’s first, and with `--local-verify` any lane touching `.github/` whose base moved); the main session never rebases or pushes Dependabot’s branch, because Dependabot stops rebasing a pull request once anyone else has pushed to it, which was item 119 (4)’s reason for not re-signing its commits. When `main` has moved by more than prose since the pull request’s base, it comments `@dependabot rebase` and waits for fresh checks; a push by Dependabot after the comment gets fresh reviews and a fresh comment. A bump that moves a golden or a chain is treated as any other movement (AGENTS.md sections 4.8 and 5): Dependabot re-blesses nothing, so the main session pushes the re-blessed files as a signed-off commit on the branch, after which Dependabot no longer rebases it, and the comment says why the hashes moved; otherwise it does not merge. The delegation stays the walking skeleton’s and the owner’s to revoke, as items 85 and 86 made it: when the owner’s review of T22’s stage demo ends the skeleton, this question goes back to the owner with the rest of the delegation. *Downsides:* two reviews for each weekly grouped bump, which moves every `uses:` line of the actions it bumps (five of `actions/checkout` in `ci.yml` alone), cost tokens; for a JavaScript action the diff between the two SHAs includes its compiled `dist/` bundle, which a review can skim but not read line by line; and a Dependabot pull request waits until the main session is up. *Rejected:* the owner merges them (the owner’s time on routine bumps, and a fix to a pinned action, already a week late at best (item 119 (4)), waits on the owner as well); merging on green checks alone (a compromised or broken upstream release would go in unread, which pinning by SHA exists to prevent).

- **Item 132, the pre-push gate (2026-10-05, #87).** The machine-wide rule (the operator’s global instructions: each repository versions a pre-push hook that runs its check before anything leaves the box, and its check fails a clone that is not wired) reached this repository by a request from the operator’s tech-stack session, which the owner confirmed here by choosing what the hook runs. `scripts/githooks/` holds the hooks, wired once per clone with `git config core.hooksPath scripts/githooks` (README, “Setting up a clone”; AGENTS.md §8): `pre-commit` wraps `scripts/pre-commit.sh`, and `pre-push` runs `cargo xtask fmt clippy` over the whole workspace, 22 s on a warm target, and refuses a push of anything but HEAD’s commit, since it checks the working tree. xtask’s `the_clone_runs_the_versioned_hooks` fails a clone whose `core.hooksPath` is not `scripts/githooks` or whose hooks are not tracked as executable, except where `CI` or `GITHUB_ACTIONS` holds a value; a `wsl-ci.sh` run of the Linux mirror, a fresh clone, passes `CI=1`, which also turns on `--locked` as in CI. `scripts/merge-train.sh` pushes in the lane’s warm target, and the lane brief forbids `--no-verify` and `PHARMAKOS_SKIP_HOOKS=1` as a way past a hook. Two departures from the global rule, both recorded here: the folder is `scripts/githooks`, the repository’s own convention, which `scripts/pre-commit.sh`’s header had planned; and the hook runs fmt and clippy, not the full check, by the owner’s choice (“fmt + clippy”). *Downside:* a failing test can still be pushed: CI’s three-OS run catches it on the branch and `main` is protected, and a lane’s builder runs the full suite before its first push, though its fix pass does not; a worktree of a commit older than #87 runs no hooks until it is rebased; and a tree with no git checkout, such as a source archive, fails the `test` step until it is set up as a clone. *Rejected:* `cargo xtask ci --quick`, measured at 1900 s on a warm target with three lanes building beside it, nearly all of it in `test`, which every rebase and docs push in the merge flow would wait on or skip; the full suite, slower still and a repeat of CI’s run; and a `.githooks/` folder beside the `scripts/` that already held the hook.
