Its lower bound is the octile cost at the rules' step costs (`Surface::heuristic`), which `nearest_is_the_least_served_walk` (`tests/nearest.rs`) asserts is never above a candidate's served walk; candidates open in octile order, and a priced candidate is emitted once its key is below every unpriced candidate's `(bound, y, x)`. So the order is exact by construction (the oracle test weighs every feature and rank on four generated or scarred maps), each candidate costs at most one priced walk, and nothing is capped: the work is bounded by the candidate count (`MAX_FEATURES`) and the router's own search. A walk the chain could not finish (`WalkError::Stalled`) is no candidate and is counted under its own reason. The ranker keeps the octile bound, not the grid optimum, by measurement: over 396 origins on scarred maps the grid optimum as the bound popped p50 / p99 / max 20,414 / 59,563 / 64,110 for a first pick against the octile's 2,364 / 10,243 / 20,098, and 162 k / 178 k / 179 k for a full ranking against 27 k / 34 k / 35 k. Ties go to the lowest site `(y, x)`; straight-line distance is not used. The legal sites are listed once per resolve (`legal_sites`), before any search: with no legal site there is no search at all, and a named target the commander cannot reach is no search either. Otherwise one search runs outward from the feature (`pathing::reach::Reach`, a bucket queue, Dial's, over the step rule read backwards, valid because the rule is symmetric: `the_step_rule_is_symmetric`), directed at the spheres that listed a site. A column's key is `cost + h`; `h` is the least, over spheres that listed at least one site, of the octile cost from the column to the sphere's centre less the sphere's reach (the most octile cost from its centre to a site it listed itself, each site being listed by one sphere), floored at zero, computed once a column when the search first reaches it. It is **admissible** (the octile cost is a metric and every step costs at least its octile length, so a walk from a column to a site costs at least `octile(column, centre) - reach`) and **consistent** (each term changes across a step by at most that step's octile length, so no key falls along a step and a column settles at its least cost, once); `the_directed_search_heuristic_is_admissible_and_consistent` holds `h`, as the production sphere list gives it, to the true cost to the nearest site on generated and scarred terrain. Every site settles at key = cost, so the first site settled is at the least cost `c`; `closest_site`, the tie-break's one home, takes the least `(cost, y, x)` among the sites settled until the key passes `c` (`the_stone_tie_goes_to_the_lowest_site_whatever_the_queue_settles_first`, in `targeting.rs`, builds ties where the queue settles the higher site first). No walk is priced. Counted work, release builds on a machine that was not idle, "undirected" being the same search with no direction: the pinned vent on the probation seed popped 937 nodes and computed 1,130 `h` in 0.7 ms (undirected 10,020 pops, 1.6 ms); the farthest vent, 24,654 pops and 25,597 `h` in 4.1 ms (106,531 pops, 15.7 ms); the farthest vent behind a long wall, the largest resolve built, 46,791 pops in 7.5 ms (110,507 pops, 16.5 ms). A resolve costs at most a full directed flood, measured at 74, 103 and 148 ms for three seats at 1, 18 and 40 spheres against 64 ms undirected, a bound no resolve reaches; a seat's most beacons list 36,513 sites over 37,653 columns in 2.5 ms (`the_site_listing_at_a_seats_most_beacons`). The undirected bucket queue settles in the order of the binary heap it replaced, `(cost, column)`, and is faster (a full flood of the shipped map 23.6 ms against 37.3 ms); the directed search does not sort a bucket and promises no order within a key, which is why `closest_site` takes the tie-break itself. Item 62's `(f, h, node_id)` order of the router's own searches is unchanged by the lane. Every millisecond figure in this point is from a release build on a machine that was not idle. The terrain is the live world's, unfogged, until S4's mask (item 168 (10)), as every other read of targeting's is (item 108 (1)). **The idle run of these figures is the main session's and is `cert3`'s to read.**

Before this pull request the text was built whole before it was hashed: `plan_fingerprint_of` wrote it into one `String` sized from the wire bytes, and `plan_fingerprint` cloned the playbook, encoded it to a `String` and copied the bytes after the domain into a second buffer. At the size budget the text is near a megabyte. The body counted the bytes each call asked the allocator for (a per-thread counting allocator, an uncommitted harness, no timed run because the machine was not idle): for `plan_fingerprint_of`, 82,963 / 482,611 / 919,395 bytes before and 19,520 / 40,640 / 61,120 after, with the largest single request falling from 71,635 / 450,163 / 866,467 to 8,192, for `budget_128` (33,229 B of canonical text), the P1 handler shape (431,571 B) and the P1 route shape (850,014 B). `plan_fingerprint(&Playbook)` fell from 179,456 / 1,760,776 / 3,387,158 to 146,189 / 1,329,167 / 2,537,106. The codec's work meter reads the same bytes before and after.
  - **(2) The design, as built.** (a) `StreamingDigest` (`crates/sim/src/encoding.rs`) wraps xxh3's own streaming state seeded with `STATE_HASH_SEED`: no new dependency or feature, a fixed inline state, no allocation; `digest` is unchanged. (b) `write_wire_into` (`crates/proto/src/json/codec.rs`) takes any `S: for<'t> Extend<&'t str>` sink, so a `String` still works and no caller changed; the text goes through one 8 KiB gathering buffer handed on whenever the next piece would not fit, and a string past 1,365 bytes is escaped in pieces by the one escaper (`write_string`), so no string is held whole. The writer is shared with `write_wire` through a private `Out` trait, so `json::encode` pays no copy and the two writers cannot write different text; the buffer size is a validated `Limit`. (c) `plan_fingerprint_of` (`crates/sim/src/hash.rs`) feeds the domain and the codec's pieces to the digest and never builds the text; `text_capacity`, `TEXT_PER_WIRE_BYTE` and `MAX_TEXT_HINT` are gone (a search of the code finds none). `plan_fingerprint` hashes through the same digest without the second buffer, but still encodes the message whole, because the sim has no way to a message's wire bytes. (d) The verifier's decode stage (`crates/verifier/src/decode.rs`) now computes the fingerprint through `plan_fingerprint_of` on every path, its fallback after a `decode_json_encoded` included; before, that fallback called `plan_fingerprint`. The codec's work meter (`json::work`) now counts each piece as it goes out, not the text once at the end: equal on success (`the_work_counted_is_the_text_both_ways`), and a write that fails part-way leaves the pieces already handed on counted.

To test against the old code, a lane commits its work first and adds a detached scratch worktree at the old commit, or saves a patch with `git diff` and restores it with `git apply`.   - **(1) What it supersedes, by quotation.** Item 164 (3a) wrote: "The main session plans a change to the check so that such a file fails the `reuse` step, which would make a forgotten header go red; that change does not exist yet, and until it does the record is all there is." **That change now exists.** The check fails the `reuse` step for a file that carries the library's licence and quotes nothing, so a `host.rs` whose `SAFE_PLAYBOOK` copy goes but whose header does not return to `GPL-3.0-or-later` alone goes red.
  - **(2) The union rule.** The check takes the union of the licence identifiers across every expression `reuse` reports for a file, operators dropped. A tracked file outside `library/` fails when its union holds `GPL-3.0-or-later`, `MIT` and `Apache-2.0` and it quotes nothing of the library. That covers the combined form in any spelling, the licences split across sources (a manifest block's `GPL-3.0-or-later` beside the header's `MIT OR Apache-2.0`) and a fourth licence beside them. Files under `library/` are the text quoted and are not held to it. The failure lines name each of the file's expressions once and say to write `GPL-3.0-or-later` in the file's header or delete the `REUSE.toml` entry that gives it the library's licence.
  - **(3) How files are read.** Media, fonts and the descriptor set (`BINARY`: png, jpg, jpeg, gif, ico, vox, ogg, wav, mp3, ttf, otf, woff, woff2, binpb) are never read and hold no prose; one fails if its licences name all three. A tracked archive or executable (`OPAQUE`: zip, pck, wasm, dll, so, dylib, exe, bin) is `Refusal::Opaque` whatever its licence, since it can embed library text the check cannot read. **A tracked file missing from disk is `Refusal::Missing`** ("tracked and not on disk; restore it, or commit its removal"); any other read error is `Refusal::Read`. Reading is `read_tracked(names, read)`, taking the reader as a value so these are unit-tested with no filesystem. The positive control is `verdict(outcome, known)`: each `KNOWN` file must be found quoting the library and naming both licences. Decided; the owner can veto: licences compared as a set of identifiers; `binpb` with the media; one `Refusal::Misses` list for both directions.

  - **(1) The defect.** Spec section 6's Survey row says that scouts "refresh those sightings before the next Lull, so the playbook is written on fresh knowledge" (item 13; never cut, item 144 (11)). The refresh pass was a fixed last 60 s, too short for a far walk, and a sighting stopped being due once it left the reach window, though a Push is longer than the window. Every rule changed was an earlier lane's own reading, stated in neither the spec, the log nor the rules table: bugs, each fix an engineering call, **decided; the owner can veto**. The owner's two rulings are item 173 (1) and (2), "Refresh only (Recommended)" and "Refresh wins, accept losses (Recommended)".
  - **(2) The design, as the code on `main` has it** (`crates/sim/src/survey.rs`). The scouts of a seat are decided together on every decision tick, before the units' programs run (`programs::run_all` calls `survey::decide_scouts` after `defend::update` and `attack::update`; the runner's phase order is untouched). Every scout gets an ordered list of sightings, re-derived on every decision from hashed state into stack arrays sized by `world::SIGHTINGS_PER_SEAT` (64), so no list is state. A sighting is listed if it is due (at least `REFRESH_INTERVAL` old) or needed (out of the reach window at the Lull with no re-check before it); rank is needed first, then enemy beacons, then oldest, then the lowest asset id; a scout already walking to a listed sighting keeps it at its head; each other sighting goes at the end of the list it lengthens least, or, where no end keeps every needed sighting fitting, into the list and position it lengthens least (cheapest insertion at the octile bound; ties to the later position, then the lowest unit row, since the earlier position breaks S2's acceptance tests `the_stalest_sighting_is_refreshed_next` and `enemy_beacons_come_first`); no list spans more than the reach window from its first needed refresh to its last; sightings inside one remembered gun's range are split across the seat's scouts before they are chained on one; a scout departs when it is already walking, when its head is due and it has nothing to scan, in the Push's last minute, or when its list no longer leaves time (`list_leaves_time`: priced on one decision in `REPRICE_DECISIONS`, 8, and at the octile bounds alone on any other). **The seat treats every enemy beacon as an armed core**, because the gateway does not show which of another seat's beacons is its core; a forward beacon is in fact unarmed, so sightings near one are split across scouts when one could have taken them in turn, and a death near one counts as a death under a gun. Every decision loop reports its counted work to `seams::Meter` (item 175); `decide_scouts` and `run_scout` pass `()` for the Programs phase, which is outside any seat's decision (item 175 (4)).
  - **(3) The four reviews and four fix passes.** (a) **Review 1** (read `2553c1bf`): the contract review found it mergeable; the correctness review did not: a scout took over a sighting another scout was already walking to (HIGH; seed `0x2`, three seats, round 3, a beacon sighting 234 s old with two scouts alive). Fix pass 1 made the assignment joint and deterministic, kept a walking scout's sighting, and added the committed scenario `scenarios/s3/survey-keeps-a-core-fresh` with its chain (AGENTS.md section 10 item 4). The owner's "Refresh wins, accept losses" was given that day. (b) **Review 2** (read `5e4cde5c`): one scout answered for several sightings, and sightings past the free-scout count were never checked (HIGH); fix pass 2 built the ordered lists described above. (c) **Review 3** (read `1b4b523e`): two MEDIUM faults: "out of reach" was claimed for sightings that another order would reach (the rank and append-only insertion), and a scout dying on its list lost the next sighting (17 stale Lulls in 360 on seed 29 at two seats); fix pass 3 ranked needed sightings first, built cheapest insertion and the window span, split sightings under a gun, and counted the misses under enumerated reasons. (d) **Review 4** (read `cf37c8cb`): cannot merge yet; every one of the 10 stale Lulls of 360 had been labelled `OutOfReach` although each followed the death of the scout that carried the sighting, because the drop tested reach before anything else; the property test excused more than its doc said; a needed sighting under a threat the seat sees was counted nowhere; the drop log kept the last Push's drops when the current Push dropped nothing. Fix pass 4 named drops by cause, in this order: `UnderThreat` (new), `ScoutLost` (listed and fitting at an earlier decision of this Push and a scout of the seat has died since, tested before reach), `OutOfReach` (never listed and fitting, and no scout alone reaches it before the Lull) and `CrowdedOut`. "Listed earlier" and "died since" live in `survey::Memory`, in the search scratch beside the drop log: a measurement, never hashed or snapshotted, empty after a resume, read only to name a reason and by tests; the log is the running Push's.

With the margin, stale Lulls (arrangement A, two scouts) were 14 against 8, scouts lost 424 against 310, repeat deaths 156 against 66, cells explored at round 4 11,022 against 13,562; only walks priced improved (39,568 against 81,566).   - **(1) What it built.** A Lull resumed from a save reads the Push before it exactly as the live Lull did.
    - **The save format is version 4** (`SAVE_FORMAT_VERSION`), additive over 3: a required top-level `last_push` member (the feed's lines with their audience, witnesses and memo, its round, segment, anchor tick and drops since the segment ended, and the recap's record, or `lost`, or none), and a third boundary value `ended`. A version-3 save loads with `last_push` absent (`LAST_PUSH_ABSENT`), resumes as it always did and reads as `PushUnread::Resumed` in the operator; a version-4 save without the member and a version-3 save with one are refused as damaged. What a reader of a later version must do is stated: read every earlier version it can, each missing member absent and said in a typed state, never a default it cannot tell from a value, and refuse a member present in a version that never wrote it. A build before this one refuses a version-4 save. The owner's approval is item 177 (5).

Not saved, with reasons: `recycled`, `segment_failures` and the bus's absolute drop mark.

A cut part ends with `…` and is counted (`Cuts`); a diagnostic still past its bound is a typed `ReportFault`, counted as left out, never a longer report. Counts cannot overflow quietly (`ReportFault::CountPastU64`, and `CapRead` counts by grouping).

the leading sequence and tick fields are unchanged and no committed golden moved (`tests/golden/gateway/audit_log/` holds no withheld answer). `Surface::lower_answer_cap` lowers the cap for a test and never raises it. **A request `id` past 128 bytes** (`MAX_ID_BYTES`, UTF-8 bytes as read) is an Invalid Request answered under no id (`rpc::parse`). **A view is paged by bytes** (`VIEW_PAGE_BYTES` 512 KiB of chunks and entities, `listed_bytes`): the entities follow the chunks over as many pages as they need, each cut from one list held when the chunks end, so every entity is listed once and a client joins a listing's pages. **Every reader joins a listing's entities**: the client's `ViewModel::begin_listing` (told by `Answer::view_starts`), the operator, `gamectl`'s balance census and the gateway tests' `support::view`; the operator's `read_view` answers an `Option`, a view not complete within `PAGES_MAX` being **no view by type**. **The library**: `read_within` reads a file over a declared length and refuses past the playbook's text cap before a byte is asked; `library::list` returns the files it refused, typed (`Refusal`: `Unreadable`, `TooLarge`, `NotAPlaybook`) and counted by reason once a listing (`AuditLog::library_refused`); `instantiate_template` says a file past the cap in words (`INTERNAL`), no longer `NOT_FOUND`. **The client's inbound buffer is `MAX_ANSWER_FRAME_BYTES`** (the cap plus a frame's largest header, 10 bytes), passed through. **Carried 1:** a dead host's links are given up at once, in the host's own words (`Rig::host_exited`, `GaveUp`, `watch_host_exited`, `host_link.gd`'s `_tell_host_exit`), where the lobby used to wait out the reconnect budget first. **Carried 2:** the watch check's oversize legs build their oversize message on purpose, and a second leg proves a real match never meets the backstop.

  - **(1) What a transition field is, and what it replaced.** A route query joined each of its endpoints to the abstract graph by a sweep of the endpoint's whole cluster: at cluster 32 the two sweeps were 2,048 of a served walk's 2,628 grid pops (`clusters.rs`' module docs, measured over 130 walks on the golden seed). `Clusters::rebuild_intra` already sweeps the cluster from each transition cell to price its intra edges, and a step costs the same in both directions (`Surface::step_over` reads both ends, a diagonal's two sides against both, and charges a climb for any change of height, up or down), so the cost from a transition cell to a column is the cost from that column to it. The sweep's whole result is now kept as the cluster's **transition fields**: for each transition slot, a `u16` cost to every column of the cluster. `route::insert_endpoint` reads one entry a slot (`Clusters::field`) where a sweep ran before, and a cluster's fields are rebuilt exactly when its intra edges are, by the same sweep (a repair, a rebuild, a restore), so a repair leaves them what a fresh build makes. **The bound:** a cluster keeps at most `FIELDS_PER_CLUSTER` fields, 64 (16 in the lane's first commit, raised in its third by a probe of G3′-real's 8-minute segment, whose busiest cluster held 44 transition cells, and in which 16 of the 144 clusters held more than 16 from the first minute and 25 by the last); `ClusterShape::fields` is a bound, and a decomposition keeps room for the lesser of it and a cluster's most transitions, `4 * edge`. At cluster 32 on the shipped map that is 18.9 MB of derived state a world (144 clusters, 64 fields, 1,024 entries), against 4.7 MB at 16: a bound on memory, not on the game (AGENTS.md section 12), with its reason beside the constant. **Whole or none:** a cluster with more transition cells than the bound keeps no fields, and an entry's last value (`u16::MAX`) says "no walk", so a cost at that value or past it leaves its cluster with none; a cluster with none has its endpoints swept as before, and no answer depends on which a cluster has (`a_cluster_keeps_its_fields_up_to_the_bound_exactly`, `a_cost_past_a_field_entry_leaves_its_cluster_swept`, and the fields held to the sweep entry by entry and a decomposition with fields to one built with none, `ClusterShape::with_fields(0)`, query by query). An estimate's median search falls from about 2,600 pops to 601 (the body). The fields are never hashed, snapshotted or saved, and `Clusters::fingerprint()` does not move; `field_fingerprint()` is a separate figure the repair tests compare.
  - **(2) Why a field is not the cache item 61 forbids (the body's "Owed to the docs"; decided, the owner can veto).** Item 61 reads: "No estimate cache: P3-a passes with 18 % headroom and a cache is hashed state that has to be invalidated identically on every platform; a per-(start cluster, goal cluster) cache invalidated on repair stays plan §6's named P3-a fallback." A field is keyed by a cluster and one of its transition slots, never by a query's start or goal, holds no query's result, and is derived from the surface alone, like the inner edges, by the sweep that builds them and at the moment it builds them; it is a per-cluster copy of the build's own sweeps, rebuilt with the inner edges, and has nothing to invalidate that the inner edges do not. It is not hashed state, and no answer moves by a unit. The per-(start cluster, goal cluster) cache stays item 61's named fallback, unbuilt.

With the pops that is every loop of a served walk's search, so a walk's counted work no longer rests on its pops bounding the rest: an endpoint inserted by lookup pops nothing and is counted by the slots it reads. **A heap's sift is exempt, and why its bound holds**: a push follows one counted neighbour slot or abstract edge, a pop is one counted pop or stale entry, and each sifts at most the heap's depth, the base-two logarithm of its length; the bucket queue's ring walk and unlinking are counted because no pop or slot bounds them (`search.rs`' `Heap` docs). **`Scratch::queue` and `Scratch::queue_abstract` are the one way into a heap** (they record and push, both or neither) and **`Scratch::pop_open` and `Scratch::pop_open_abstract` the one way out**, each stale entry skipped counted once there. The count stays a measurement: nothing reads it to decide, and it is never hashed.   - **(1) The certification opt-in.** A run is certifying only when it is asked: `PHARMAKOS_BENCH_CERTIFY` (`provenance::CERTIFY_VAR`), read strictly by `provenance::certify_from`: unset is not certifying, exactly `1` is, and any other value refuses the run (`Error::Plan`), so a typo never runs as either. It is one variable for every certifying command, and the owner's recorded runs set it. `PHARMAKOS_BENCH_CERT_CALLS` (`provenance::CERT_CALLS_VAR`) only cuts P1's timed calls a figure, and a cut run never certifies, whatever the first variable says. **No workflow sets either**, and xtask's `no_workflow_asks_a_bench_run_to_certify` holds that over `.github/workflows/**`. Every line a certifying command prints ends with its sampling stamp (`provenance::stamped`), whose counts are read from what ran and never from the plan (P1's calls; P3's seeds and the fewest samples any figure took; the kinds' fewest runs and ticks; G3′'s ticks played), in one of three forms: `[certifying: …]` only when the run was asked and no count is cut, `[NOT A CERTIFYING FIGURE: not a certifying run (PHARMAKOS_BENCH_CERTIFY unset); …]`, or `[NOT A CERTIFYING FIGURE: a count is cut from its plan; …]`. One predicate decides whether a line certifies (`provenance::is_certifying`), every command's lines are assembled in `certify` (`p1_lines`, `p3_lines`, `kinds_lines`, `watch_lines`, `raids_lines`), and harness tests that are not ignored run every line of a cut run of each, asked and not asked, through the predicate. A P1 run that ends in a refusal certifies no line (`P1Run::stamp`, `a_failed_runs_lines_never_speak_as_evidence`). Every certifying command names its commit and says when tracked files differ from it (`provenance::commit`).

  - **(4) The idle status, and the poll's 16 false marks.** All 42 runs read idle before and after. The during-run poll was rewritten after item 223 (4)'s finding: it looks 3 s in and every 15 s, includes `cargo.exe` and `xtask.exe`, and tells the run's own processes from foreign ones by the process tree. In 26 runs it saw no foreign build process. **In the other 16, all on Windows, it marked the run's own processes FOREIGN, and nothing else.** They are exactly the 16 Windows runs whose command starts with `env PHARMAKOS_BENCH_CERTIFY=1 cargo ...`: under MSYS the chain bash, then `env`, then `cargo` leaves cargo's parent process id pointing at a process that has exited, so the tree walk could not tie cargo and the test binary to the wrapper. **The mechanical check** (`D:/build/cert/tools/checkmarks.sh`): in each of the 16 records every sample lists exactly two processes, one `cargo.exe` and the one test binary that record's own "Running" line names, with the same two process ids through the run; at each of its samples (3 s in, then every 15 s) nothing else appeared; the idle checks before and after each run cover the ends; a build that started and ended between two samples would not show (`windows-p1cap-1` and `windows-p1decision-1` hold one sample each, `windows-g3s2-1` three). **The fix:** the wrapper (`run.sh`) applies a leading `env K=V` in its own shell. **The rehearsal:** the same P3 command under the fixed wrapper reads "no foreign build process seen" (`D:/build/cert/rehearsal-poll/windows-p3-rehearsal.txt`; a rehearsal, counted nowhere). **Decided: the 16 runs stand and are not retaken; the owner can veto** (a retake of the Windows leg is 40 minutes). The WSL2 leg's commands do not go through MSYS `env` on the Windows side and carry no mark. The lesson: rehearse a changed wrapper before a certifying leg.
